nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.urodevmedical.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/urodev-medical

UroDev Medical, operating under the brand Spinal Singularity, develops connected medical devices designed to improve the quality of life for individuals with Spinal Cord Injury and Disease (SCI/D). The company focuses on addressing specific medical needs through technology that integrates connectivity with clinical care.

Its first product, the Connected Catheter, aims to revolutionize the management of Neurogenic Bladder and Urinary Incontinence. By targeting these conditions, the company sought to provide a more effective solution for patients dealing with the complications of spinal cord injuries.

UroDev Medical was based in San Clemente, California, and has since been acquired.

"The Connected Catheter is a connected medical device specifically designed to manage Neurogenic Bladder and Urinary Incontinence in people with Spinal Cord Injury and Disease, whereas standard catheters are typically passive tools without integrated connectivity features."

Mecha Health creates proprietary foundation models that process medical images and generate draft radiology reports. Its first model was built in under two months and outperformed Microsoft, Google, and OpenAI on clinical accuracy metrics while being two orders of magnitude smaller and trained on only a quarter of the data.

The company partners with the largest privately owned radiology practice in the United States and a multinational tele‑radiology firm, giving them dedicated models that let radiologists read a scan every five minutes instead of one per hour. By charging per scan, Mecha Health targets a market opportunity estimated at over $40 billion. The team of four operates out of San Francisco, California.

_Usage:_

"How can Mecha Health claim higher clinical accuracy than Microsoft, Google, and OpenAI while using a model that’s much smaller and trained on less data?"

"Mecha Health says its proprietary models are specifically engineered for x‑ray analysis, allowing it to achieve higher clinical accuracy on that task even though the models are two orders of magnitude smaller and trained with only a quarter of the data used by the larger tech firms."

nodes.title: Hera
nodes.description: Hera automates motion graphics creation, turning multi‑hour projects into minutes. YC S25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://hera.video/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/hera-video

Hera is an AI motion designer that transforms five‑hour animation projects into five‑minute tasks. It was launched in May 2025 and quickly attracted 100 k waitlist sign‑ups within eight weeks. By focusing on the 95 % of motion‑graphics work that consists of manual button clicking, Hera automates the tedious steps while preserving full creative control for users such as YouTubers creating infographic animations. The Berlin‑based team of five has been doubling revenue each month, positioning Hera as a fast‑growing B2B tool for engineering, product, and design teams.

_Usage:_

"Does Hera replace Adobe After Effects for creating infographic animations?"

"Hera doesn’t replace the creative capabilities of After Effects but automates the repetitive button‑clicking steps. For a typical YouTuber, the same animation that would take hours in After Effects can be produced in minutes with Hera, while still allowing the user to control the visual outcome."

nodes.title: Fini
nodes.description: Fini builds AI agents that automate up to 80% of enterprise customer support tickets. YC S22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.usefini.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fini

Fini creates AI agents that autonomously resolve up to 80% of support tickets for enterprises in fintech, e‑commerce, gaming and fitness tech. The agents understand complex workflows, can take real actions such as refunds or KYC checks, and improve in real time thanks to a proprietary knowledge engine that delivers over 98% accuracy. They integrate deeply with tools like Zendesk, Salesforce and internal APIs.

Enterprises such as Bitdefender and Training Peaks use Fini to cut support costs by about half while raising customer satisfaction scores by roughly 10%. The company operates with a 14‑person team out of Amsterdam, Netherlands, and serves B2B operations customers through a SaaS model.

_Usage:_

"How is Fini’s AI agent different from a regular chatbot that’s hooked up to Zendesk?"

"Fini’s agents go beyond simple text responses: they can execute real actions like processing refunds or performing KYC checks, and they continuously learn to improve accuracy, which the company reports exceeds 98%. By using a proprietary knowledge engine and deep integrations with Zendesk, Salesforce and internal APIs, the agents can resolve most tickets end‑to‑end without human hand‑off, whereas a typical chatbot would usually need escalation for those tasks."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.dili.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dili

Dili (YC S23) is creating a reliable AI system of record that helps physical‑industry companies track compliance, analyze labor and spend, and run payroll. It has already run prevailing‑wage, apprenticeship, and other labor‑compliance programs across energy, infrastructure, datacenters, advanced manufacturing, and construction, enabling customers to secure more than $1 billion in federal funding.

The company positions its AI platform as the most dependable automation for compliance in real‑world industries, aiming to replace manual processes with a continuously updated, data‑driven solution. With a team of 15 engineers in New York City, Dili serves B2B customers in finance and accounting, energy, and related sectors.

_Usage:_

"How does Dili’s AI compliance platform differ from traditional compliance software?"

"Traditional compliance tools often require manual data entry and periodic audits, whereas Dili’s AI continuously records compliance actions, automatically runs prevailing‑wage and apprenticeship checks, and integrates payroll and spend analysis, allowing customers to maintain real‑time compliance and qualify for large federal funding programs."

nodes.title: Fragment
nodes.description: Fragment turns manual fintech operations into scalable AI‑human workflows. YC S23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://checkfragment.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fragment

Fragment builds software that bridges AI and human workers, based on the premise that every AI‑enabled company will need humans in the loop for handoff tasks. It initially targets operations teams in fintech firms, providing task‑management tools for manual processes such as onboarding and compliance. By layering human supervision on top of these workflows, Fragment makes it easy for companies to increase automation while retaining oversight. The company was acquired, reflecting its relevance in the B2B operations space.

_Usage:_

"Will Fragment fully automate my fintech onboarding process or still require human supervision?"

"Fragment is designed to add a human‑supervision layer rather than replace humans entirely; it manages manual tasks like onboarding and compliance and then lets you incrementally automate them while keeping a human in the loop for oversight."

nodes.title: Brex
nodes.description: Provides corporate cards, business accounts, and AI-powered spend management software for startups and enterprises. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.brex.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/brex

Brex is an AI-powered spend platform that unifies corporate cards, expense management, travel, business accounts, and bill pay into a single system. Operating out of San Francisco with a team of 1,000, the platform is designed to automate manual expense workflows and enable real-time tracking across more countries and currencies than competing spend solutions. Brex was acquired.

The platform features corporate cards offering 10–20x higher limits and business accounts with $6M in FDIC insurance, same-day liquidity, and global payment capabilities. Serving tens of thousands of customers, Brex supports high-growth organizations such as DoorDash, Coinbase, ScaleAI, SeatGeek, and Superhuman.

_Usage:_

"How does Brex integrate business accounts and corporate cards into unified spend management?"

"Brex combines business accounts—offering $6M in FDIC insurance, same-day liquidity, and global payment processing—with corporate cards that feature 10-20x higher limits. Rather than relying on post-purchase expense reporting, the platform automates manual expense work, travel, and bill pay in real time within a single system."

nodes.title: Faire
nodes.description: Operates an online wholesale marketplace that uses machine learning to match local retailers with independent brands. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.faire.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/faire

Founded in the Winter 2017 YC batch, Faire operates a global wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with brand products tailored to their specific storefronts. The platform leverages machine learning and a data-driven approach to help small shops discover inventory while unburdening them from traditional retail obstacles.

To help independent stores compete with big-box chains, Faire provides straightforward financial terms that eliminate inventory risk and offer direct access to capital. For wholesale brands, the platform delivers built-in sales, marketing, and analytics tools to simplify back-office operations and customer reach.

Based in San Francisco with a team of around 900 people, Faire has built a platform supporting hundreds of thousands of retailers, resulting in over 7 million new brand-retailer connections to date.

_Usage:_

"How does Faire reduce financial risk and streamline product sourcing for local retailers?"

"Faire uses machine learning to match local store profiles with relevant brands and products. To lower the risk of trying new inventory, the platform provides access to capital and structured financial terms that eliminate inventory risk for small storefronts—offering terms that were historically only available to major big-box retailers."

nodes.title: Terark
nodes.description: Builds a database storage engine that enables direct search on highly compressed data. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.terark.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/terark

Terark developed a storage engine for databases and data systems designed to handle big data workloads. Its technology enables direct search capabilities on heavily compressed data, delivering up to 200X faster read performance and over 10X storage savings compared to engines like Google's LevelDB and Facebook's RocksDB.

Based in Beijing, the company targeted large-scale data applications looking to lower costs while increasing performance. Terark participated in the Winter 2017 Y Combinator batch, counted Alibaba among its paying customers, and has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does Terark compare to standard storage engines like RocksDB or LevelDB?"

"Terark's key distinction is its ability to perform direct searches on compressed data. This design provides over 10X better storage savings and up to 200X faster read performance compared to engines like Facebook's RocksDB and Google's LevelDB."

nodes.title: Pachama
nodes.description: Restoring nature to solve climate change. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://pachama.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pachama

Pachama is a climate‑tech company that leverages computer vision and satellite imagery to verify reforestation and conservation projects, ensuring they sequester carbon, enhance biodiversity, and benefit local communities.

Through a tech‑verified marketplace, Pachama channels capital from corporate clients such as Amazon, Airbnb, Netflix, and Nespresso into forests across Brazil, Mexico, India, and the United States. The company’s platform provides transparent, data‑driven proof of carbon removal, attracting backing from investors like Bill Gates’ BEV, Chis Sacca’s LowerCarbon, and the Amazon Climate Pledge.

Pachama was acquired in 2024, and it operates fully remote with a team of 85 based in San Francisco, CA, and worldwide.

_Usage:_

"How does Pachama verify the carbon sequestration of its reforestation projects?"

"Pachama uses computer vision algorithms on satellite imagery to monitor forest growth and calculate the amount of carbon sequestered, providing a data‑driven verification that its projects meet the claimed environmental impact."

nodes.title: Dropprint Genomics
nodes.description: Dropprint Genomics delivers cost-effective single-cell genomics software that scales analysis of millions of immune cells. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://dropprintgen.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dropprint-genomics

Dropprint Genomics writes software that decodes the activity of individual cells instead of averaging signals across populations. By focusing on single-cell resolution, the company can pinpoint rare cell states that are invisible to bulk assays. The platform was built by a team that was the first to process and analyze millions of immune cells, and it now hosts a database of over one million immune cells spanning healthy, cancerous, and autoimmune states. Dropprint Genomics cut the cost of single-cell sequencing tenfold and built scalable computational infrastructure to handle the data deluge. Its machine‑learning software turns the growing database into a data‑centric engine for target discovery, delivering more precise, unbiased, and automated insights for drug discovery. Dropprint Genomics was acquired.

"How does Dropprint Genomics reduce the cost of single-cell sequencing?"

"By optimizing computational pipelines and scaling infrastructure, Dropprint Genomics cuts costs tenfold, making single-cell analysis more affordable."

nodes.body:

Metaplane is a data observability platform designed to ensure that business data is reliable and trusted. It helps data teams prevent and detect issues before they escalate into major incidents, such as incorrect revenue reports reaching executive leadership. The company was acquired, marking its exit from the YC ecosystem.

The platform utilizes machine learning for anomaly detection and provides end-to-end column-level lineage to monitor the entire data stack. Users can set up monitoring for their infrastructure within 30 minutes, allowing them to identify root causes and prevent future data incidents.

Based in New York City, Metaplane serves B2B engineering and product teams. Notable users include Bose, Ramp, and Klaviyo, who rely on the platform to maintain data integrity across their operations.

"How does Metaplane differ from standard logging or monitoring tools?"

"Metaplane focuses specifically on data quality and lineage rather than just system health. It uses ML to detect anomalies in the data itself and tracks column-level lineage across the stack, which helps teams pinpoint exactly where a data issue originated before it affects downstream business metrics."

nodes.title: Volumetric
nodes.description: Volumetric uses 3D bioprinting to create living human tissues with blood vessel networks for drug testing and organ replacement. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://volumetricbio.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/volumetric

Volumetric is a biotech company based in Houston, Texas, that develops living multicellular tissues using breakthrough 3D bioprinting technologies. The company, which was acquired after its founding in 2018, focuses on replicating discrete functions of the human body to improve basic mechanistic biology, laboratory testing, and drug development. Its technology, featured on the cover of Science, enables the creation of human tissues with complex blood vessel networks.

In the short term, Volumetric leverages this bioprinting capability to build patient-specific tissues for drug safety and efficacy testing. The process involves taking patient cells from a biopsy, integrating them into proprietary 3D printed tissues, and injecting drug compounds through the blood vessel network to mimic actual human drug delivery. This approach aims to provide rigorous, reproducible, and predictive outcomes for diseases such as cancer.

The long-term vision for the company is to produce functional tissue and organ replacements for vital organs, including the lung, liver, pancreas, kidney, and heart, using the patient's own cells. As a small team of five, the company operates at the intersection of healthcare and industrial bio, seeking to drastically improve patient outcomes through advanced tissue engineering.

_Usage:_

"How does Volumetric's bioprinting approach differ from standard 2D cell culture in drug testing?"

"Standard 2D cell cultures lack the structural complexity of real human tissue, often leading to poor predictions of drug safety and efficacy. Volumetric's method uses 3D bioprinting to create tissues with actual blood vessel networks, allowing drug compounds to be injected and delivered in a way that mimics the human body. This results in more reproducible and predictive outcomes compared to traditional laboratory testing methods."

nodes.title: Orchata
nodes.description: Groceries and daily essentials delivered in 20 minutes across Latin America. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.orchata.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/orchata

Orchata is a consumer app that provides 20-minute delivery of groceries, fresh produce, alcohol, pharmacy items, and top e-commerce brands in Latin America. The company operates an all-in-one software platform for managing darkstores located around cities, aiming to replicate the rapid growth model established by Gopuff in the United States.

Launched in Mexico, the service grew from zero to $6.3M in revenue with over 30,000 customers. It targeted the massive $451B Latin American grocery market, which was transitioning online at a rapid pace. The company maintained a team of 50 based in Monterrey, Mexico.

Orchata is currently listed as Inactive, indicating the company has since shut down.

_Usage:_

"How does Orchata's darkstore model compare to traditional grocery delivery?"

"Orchata uses an all-in-one software stack to manage a network of darkstores positioned around the city, which allows it to promise 20-minute delivery for a wide range of items including fresh meat, alcohol, and pharmacy goods. This approach mirrors the Gopuff playbook in the US, focusing on speed and a no-substitute policy at supermarket prices, rather than relying on centralized warehouses or third-party courier networks that typically have longer lead times."

nodes.title: Easyplan
nodes.description: An AI-driven investment app for beginner investors in India. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://easyplan.in/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/easyplan

Easyplan is an AI-driven investment platform designed for beginner investors in India, functioning similarly to US-based services like Betterment and Qapital. The company launched with money market funds and utilized conversational AI to help users build diversified mutual fund portfolios tailored to their specific goals. It also offers a credit card secured by user investments, allowing customers to maintain liquidity while earning returns.

The service targets the large segment of middle-income Indian workers who save significantly but lack access to simplified investment tools, as existing apps are often too complex for beginners. Easyplan achieved approximately 40,000 customers with a cost of acquisition that was 10% of the industry average, growing its assets under management threefold since April 2020.

Despite its early traction and focus on a $325B potential market, Easyplan is now inactive, indicating the company has since shut down.

_Usage:_

"How does Easyplan simplify investing for beginners compared to traditional Indian brokerage apps?"

"Instead of presenting users with over 16,000 mutual funds and 5,000 stocks, Easyplan uses conversational AI to generate diversified portfolios based on user goals. It also offers a credit card secured by these investments, which allows users to spend against their portfolio value without selling assets, effectively combining investment returns with liquidity."

nodes.title: Exosonic, Inc.
nodes.description: Developing supersonic UAVs as a pathway to quiet supersonic flight. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://exosonic.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/exosonic-inc

Exosonic, an early-stage aerospace startup based in Los Angeles, developed supersonic adversary air UAVs to support adversary air training missions for commercial and government customers. The company aimed to mature these unmanned vehicles into loyal wingmen or collaborative combat aircraft, with the long-term goal of applying lessons learned to develop quiet supersonic airliners.

Founded in 2019, the team of 14-15 FTEs raised over $4.5M in private capital and $2M in AFWERX funding. They were developing a subscale flight test vehicle designed to demonstrate autonomy and crewed-uncrewed teaming, with a first flight targeted for Q2 2023. Exosonic has since become inactive.

_Usage:_

"How does Exosonic's approach to supersonic flight differ from traditional jet development?
"

"Instead of jumping straight to passenger aircraft, Exosonic focused on building supersonic UAVs for military training first. This strategy allowed them to generate revenue and refine autonomous flight and teaming technologies before attempting the more complex engineering challenges of quiet supersonic airliners."

nodes.title: Triomics
nodes.description: Task-driven AI agents embedded in oncology EHRs to automate manual review of unstructured patient records. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://triomics.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/triomics

Triomics builds AI infrastructure for modern oncology by replacing manual staff work with task-driven AI agents embedded directly into clinical workflows. The platform automatically processes unstructured patient records, including pathology reports, clinical notes, genomic panels, and scanned faxes, in real time to support clinical trial matching, visit preparation, and quality reporting.

The New York City-based company serves a team of 50 and is trusted by four of the top 10 Best Hospitals for Cancer ranked by U.S. News, as well as several of the largest community oncology practices in the United States.

_Usage:_

"How does Triomics handle unstructured data like scanned faxes and clinical notes in oncology workflows?"

"It uses task-driven AI agents embedded directly into the EHR to automatically process these unstructured records in real time, eliminating the need for highly trained staff to manually review them for tasks like clinical trial matching and quality reporting."

nodes.title: Rethoric
nodes.description: a LinkedIn content consultancy and scheduling platform that manages the entire content operation for busy founders. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://rethoric.com/ycombinator | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rethoric

Rethoric operates as a LinkedIn content consultancy and scheduling platform designed for companies seeking to maintain visibility with their ideal customer profile without dedicating internal resources to social media management. The service handles the full content lifecycle, from strategy to publishing, for a client base that includes over 100 startups and enterprises such as Checkr, ClickUp, Storylane, and Checkly.

The platform is built to replace traditional agency workflows that rely on disjointed tools like Google Docs and scattered review threads. By integrating directly with LinkedIn and Slack, Rethoric presents content that is already written, scheduled, and ready for publication, streamlining the process for its users.

_Usage:_

"How does Rethoric differ from just hiring a freelance social media manager or using a standard scheduling tool like Buffer?"

"Rethoric combines the strategic oversight of a consultancy with a unified platform that replaces the fragmented agency workflow of docs and review threads. Instead of just scheduling posts, it manages the entire operation from strategy to publishing, with content appearing in your Slack and LinkedIn already written and ready to go, which is distinct from simple scheduling tools that require you to create the content yourself."

nodes.title: Remora
nodes.description: Carbon capture technology for trains and trucks that extracts and sells CO2 from exhaust. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.remoracarbon.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/remora

Remora builds carbon capture systems specifically designed for heavy-duty vehicles like trains and trucks. The company generates revenue by extracting, purifying, and selling CO2 from vehicle exhaust, while simultaneously reducing soot, particulate matter, and NOx emissions. Remora’s technology claims to capture up to 90% of the CO2 in the exhaust stream.

The Detroit-based team, which includes 45 employees, has established partnerships with major logistics and rail companies including Union Pacific, Norfolk Southern, Ryder, and Werner. Remora has raised $117 million from investors such as Lowercarbon Capital, Valor Equity Partners, Union Square Ventures, and Y Combinator.

_Usage:_

"How does Remora make money from carbon capture on trucks and trains?"

"Remora installs capture technology on the vehicles, extracts the CO2 from the exhaust, purifies it, and then sells that captured carbon to buyers. This creates a revenue stream for the railroads and trucking companies that host the equipment, effectively turning a waste product into a commodity while also reducing other pollutants like soot and NOx."

nodes.title: Care Weather
nodes.description: Collects high-accuracy global weather data using low-cost flat-panel radar satellites. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.careweather.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/care-weather

Care Weather operates a unique flat-panel radar satellite designed to capture the highest-accuracy global weather data. The system is vertically integrated, which makes it 1000 times more cost-effective than traditional alternatives, while also generating more solar power and sailing on top of the atmosphere for a closer view of the Earth's surface. This technology enables governments and shipping companies to better adapt to extreme weather events.

The company built and launched the smallest radar satellite ever in just four months. Based in Orem, Utah, Care Weather has secured $35 million worth of letters of intent from clients including the Air Force and various cargo shippers. The startup is backed by investors such as Boost VC, Kickstart Seed Fund, and Y Combinator.

_Usage:_

"How does Care Weather's flat-panel design achieve such significant cost savings compared to standard radar satellites?"

"The satellite is vertically integrated, which reduces manufacturing complexity and costs. Additionally, the flat-panel configuration allows the craft to collect more solar power and operate at a higher altitude, providing a closer and more direct view of the surface without the expense of traditional bulky satellite structures."

nodes.title: Mindee
nodes.description: Mindee provides an AI document understanding API that allows developers to automate the extraction and processing of data from various document types. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mindee.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mindee

Mindee offers a universal self-service platform designed to help software builders automate the understanding of documents through deep learning. The company focuses on providing a single API that grants applications the ability to process document content with human-like accuracy, addressing a critical step in automation across multiple industries.

The platform operates on three main pillars: a self-service environment where users can train their own models, a catalog of pre-built use cases optimized for critical markets like accounting, AP automation, expense management, and KYC, and an internal capability to develop tailor-made AI solutions for large customers with specific needs.

With a team of approximately 60 people, Mindee is based in Paris, San Francisco, and London. It serves the B2B sector by providing developer tools and APIs focused on automation and artificial intelligence.

_Usage:_

"How does Mindee differ from a standard OCR library?"

"While standard OCR libraries focus primarily on recognizing text characters, Mindee provides a higher-level API for document understanding. It uses deep learning to not just read the text but to interpret the context and structure of the document, allowing developers to extract specific data points relevant to use cases like KYC or expense management without building custom models from scratch."

nodes.title: Sivo
nodes.description: Debt-as-a-service API enabling fintechs and platforms to lend at scale without raising capital. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://sivo.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/sivo

Sivo provides a debt-as-a-service platform that allows fintechs, neobanks, and gig platforms to lend money to their users at scale. By offering an API and risk protocol, the company helps these businesses avoid the lengthy process of raising debt, which can take up to two years. Sivo positions itself as the "Stripe for Debt" in this space.

The company is active and has secured a $100m debt capital partnership, with plans to launch its API in April. It reports having over 100 companies in its customer pipeline, including Uber. Sivo is a 15-person team based in Vancouver, San Francisco, and remote locations, with members drawing on experience from firms like Goldman Sachs, Revolut, and Citigroup.

_Usage:_

Encord serves as the data infrastructure for physical AI, enabling teams to transform messy, multimodal datasets into production-ready systems. It supports a wide range of applications, including humanoid robots, autonomous vehicles, and smart infrastructure.

The platform focuses on curating, managing, and aligning the specific data required for model training. Over 300 teams, including Toyota, Skydio, and Maxar, rely on Encord to handle their data workflows.

nodes.title: Flux Auto
nodes.description: Building physical AI to automate material movement in warehouses and factories using legacy vehicle fleets. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://fluxauto.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/flux-auto

Flux Auto develops physical AI solutions that automate material handling in industrial settings by retrofitting existing legacy vehicle fleets. The company’s technology allows businesses to reduce reliance on human drivers while simultaneously boosting productivity and lowering operating costs. By leveraging autonomous driving capabilities for internal logistics, Flux addresses the inefficiencies inherent in manual material movement within large-scale facilities.

The company is currently deploying its systems with major industrial clients including Walmart, Daimler, Bajaj, Cummins, and Mahindra Logistics. These deployments span various environments such as warehouses, fulfillment centers, and factories. Based in Bengaluru, India, Flux Auto operates with a team of 56 people focused on the intersection of robotics and artificial intelligence.

_Usage:_

"How does Flux Auto handle the transition from manual to autonomous driving in existing facilities?"

"Flux Auto works with legacy vehicle fleets already present in warehouses and factories, applying physical AI to automate their movement rather than requiring customers to purchase new autonomous hardware. This approach allows companies to modernize their material handling operations and reduce dependency on human drivers without replacing their current fleet infrastructure."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.gromo.in | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/gromo

GroMo is building India's largest financial products distribution company by operating a tech-enabled social commerce platform. The company has assembled a network of 1.2 million independent agents who use the platform to sell financial products to consumers.

The platform is designed to bridge the financial literacy gap, helping agents guide consumers toward the right offerings. GroMo currently distributes over 100 financial products, including insurance, investments, credit cards, loans, and savings accounts, from brands such as IDFC Bank, Jupiter Money, Axis Bank, and Freecharge.

It specifically targets the financial literacy gap by equipping these agents to help consumers choose the right offerings from a catalog of over 100 products across insurance, investments, and credit."

nodes.title: Pyroscope
nodes.description: Open source continuous profiling platform for debugging performance issues. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://pyroscope.io/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pyroscope

Pyroscope is an open source continuous profiling platform designed to help engineers debug performance issues and identify bottlenecks in their code. The tool integrates with applications using just a few lines of code, providing visibility into system performance without requiring significant architectural changes.

The company was based in San Francisco and Oakland, California, and operated as a small team of five engineers. It focused on the B2B market, specifically serving engineering and product design teams through its SaaS and open source offerings.

Pyroscope was acquired, marking the end of its independent operation as a YC-backed startup.

_Usage:_

"How does Pyroscope differ from traditional APM tools or manual profiling?"

"Pyroscope focuses on continuous profiling, which allows you to constantly monitor performance bottlenecks rather than just capturing snapshots when things break. It’s designed to be lightweight, requiring only a few lines of code to integrate, so you can find performance issues in your code without the overhead of more complex observability stacks."

nodes.title: Enable Us

nodes.title: TechBiz
nodes.description: Mobile-first MIS and business intelligence tools for small businesses in India. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.techbiz.app | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/techbiz

TechBiz provides an app-first Management Information System (MIS) and Business Intelligence solution designed specifically for small and medium enterprises in India. The platform addresses the challenge of business data being trapped in hard-to-access accounting software by allowing users to track essential metrics such as debtors, creditors, sales, and outstanding balances directly on mobile devices.

The company operates as a B2B SaaS provider with a small team of three members based in New Delhi and remote locations. By simplifying access to financial data, TechBiz helps business owners make quicker and more informed decisions. The company has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does TechBiz handle the data integration problem for Indian SMEs who rely on legacy accounting software?"

"It acts as an app-first layer on top of existing accounting systems, pulling out key metrics like debtors, creditors, and sales into a mobile interface. Instead of forcing users to dig through complex desktop accounting tools, it surfaces the essential business data needed for quick decision-making directly on their phones."

nodes.title: Trendpop
nodes.description: Analytics platform that analyzes short-form video data to help brands and creators go viral on social platforms. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://trendpop.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/trendpop

Trendpop is a data-first analytics and insights platform designed to help users understand and leverage the recommendation algorithms that drive virality on short-form video platforms. The company’s core engine has collected and analyzed over a billion social video posts using state-of-the-art algorithms to identify emerging trends as they happen.

Founded in August 2020, Trendpop grew to profitability within twelve months of its YC W21 batch. In January 2022, the company was acquired by Collab, a veteran digital creator platform and official TikTok creative and marketing partner.

Following the acquisition, Trendpop powers TikTok marketing programs for major North American record labels and is expanding into the film, television, beauty, and DTC eCommerce industries. It is currently used by marketing and A&R professionals in the music industry, as well as hundreds of brands and creators, to consistently win on social video.

_Usage:_

"How does Trendpop actually predict what will go viral instead of just showing past data?"

"It doesn't just look at historical metrics; its core engine ingests over a billion social video posts and applies state-of-the-art algorithms to reverse-engineer the recommendation systems that power virality. This allows it to surface trends in real-time, helping users like music labels and brands understand the specific mechanics driving current engagement on platforms like TikTok."

nodes.title: Verak
nodes.description: Providing next-day business insurance for Indian MSMEs with satellite underwriting and ML pricing. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://verak.in | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/verak

Verak was a Bengaluru-based startup that offered business insurance to micro, small, and medium enterprises in India. The company provided next-day coverage starting at ₹8 per day, protecting facilities such as shops, warehouses, and factories against more than 15 natural and man-made perils.

The team operated across the entire insurance value chain, utilizing satellite-based underwriting and machine learning for pricing. They streamlined the user experience with instant quotations and a WhatsApp-based claims process.

Verak was acquired by InsuranceDekho in April 2023.

_Usage:_

"How did Verak handle underwriting and claims for small businesses?"

"They used satellite imagery for underwriting and machine learning to price policies, which allowed them to offer instant quotations. For claims, they relied on a WhatsApp-based process, making it accessible for MSMEs who might not have traditional insurance infrastructure."

nodes.title: Orbillion Bio
nodes.description: Orbillion Bio produces scalable cultivated beef using computational models and proprietary bioware to achieve price parity. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.orbillion.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/orbillion-bio

Orbillion Bio develops cultivated beef at scale by leveraging advanced computational models to optimize its bioprocess. The company utilizes proprietary bioware to precisely control the microenvironment required for meat cell growth, eliminating the need for GMOs, serum, or expensive growth factors. This approach enables a production cost of $4 per kg at commercial scale.

The technology addresses the primary industry challenges of cost and scale-up through an integrated bioprocess platform. This system allows for asset-light production anywhere globally within two weeks. Orbillion Bio has formed partnerships with two global food companies and a European partner to fast-track commercialization in the ground beef market.

Orbillion Bio has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does Orbillion Bio achieve such low costs for cultivated beef compared to traditional methods?"

"They use computational models to rapidly optimize the bioprocess and proprietary bioware to control the cell microenvironment. This setup supercharges cell growth without relying on GMOs, serum, or expensive growth factors, which drives the cost down to $4 per kg at commercial scale."

nodes.title: Promoted.ai
nodes.description: Unifies search, native ads, and feed ranking for online marketplaces using AI. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.promoted.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/promoted

Promoted.ai provides a unified platform for search, native advertising, and feed ranking designed for online marketplaces and scaled e-commerce applications. By leveraging AI, the company aims to dramatically improve relevance and revenue for its users. The team consists of twelve engineers based in Seattle, WA, with backgrounds at Google, Meta, and Pinterest.

The company serves publicly traded and late-stage marketplace companies, including Eventbrite, Upwork, and Outschool. Its mission is to connect every buyer and seller by enhancing the efficiency of these digital marketplaces.

Promoted.ai was acquired, marking the conclusion of its independent operation as a YC-backed startup.

_Usage:_

"How does Promoted.ai differ from building search and ads in-house?"

"Instead of maintaining separate systems for search, ads, and feed ranking, Promoted.ai unifies them into a single AI-driven stack. This approach is designed to improve relevance and revenue simultaneously, which is particularly useful for marketplace companies that need to balance buyer discovery with seller monetization without the overhead of building and maintaining distinct infrastructure for each function."

nodes.title: FunctionUp (FanPlay)
nodes.description: A technical placement bootcamp that trains talent with zero upfront fees and places them at partner companies. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.functionup.org/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/functionup-fanplay

FunctionUp, also known as FanPlay, operates a skill-tech platform focused on technical placement bootcamps. The company utilizes an Income Sharing Model, allowing it to train top tech talent without charging any upfront fees. Upon completion of the program, graduates are placed across the company's network of partner companies.

Based in Bengaluru, India, FunctionUp combines technical training with a strong social impact mission. The program provides specific assistance to women and unemployed youth in India, supporting them both economically and socially. The company was part of the Y Combinator Winter 2021 batch and has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does the Income Sharing Model work for students joining FunctionUp?"

"Students pay zero upfront fees to join the bootcamp. Instead, the cost is tied to their future earnings, as the company places them at partner companies after training. This structure removes the financial barrier to entry for top tech talent while aligning the provider's incentives with successful job placement."

nodes.title: Avenue
nodes.description: Avenue provides an observability platform that lets operations teams set up alerts directly on their databases and data warehouses. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://avenue.app/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/avenue

Avenue is an observability platform designed to help business and operations teams create simple, set-and-forget alerts directly from their existing data sources. By allowing users to monitor nuanced triggers that might not fit on a standard dashboard, the tool aims to make teams more proactive in their daily operations.

The platform focuses on improving response times to critical problems, potentially reducing detection windows from several days to real-time. It functions as a specialized alternative to broader monitoring tools, specifically tailored for those who need to alert on the data they already manage in their warehouses or databases.

Founded in Winter 2021 and based in New York City, Avenue was acquired, marking its exit from the active startup scene.

_Usage:_

"How does Avenue differ from standard monitoring tools like Datadog or PagerDuty?"

"Avenue is positioned as a simpler, more direct way to set up alerts specifically on your database or data warehouse. While tools like Datadog or PagerDuty are often broader in scope, Avenue focuses on letting operations teams create set-and-forget alerts on nuanced data triggers that might not be visible on a standard dashboard, aiming to cut response times from days to real-time."

nodes.title: Warp
nodes.description: Warp is an AI-native employee management platform that handles payroll, HR, compliance, benefits, and IT for high‑growth companies. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.warp.co/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/warp

Warp provides a single platform that runs payroll, HR, compliance, benefits, and IT for companies ranging from five to ten thousand employees, using AI agents to complete work that legacy systems leave to people.
The service is aimed at high‑growth companies that want to reduce HR and admin overhead so they can build faster. Warp counts fast‑growing startups such as Serval, Bland, Greptile, Reducto, Corgi and Campfire among its customers, as well as mid‑size and enterprise firms.

The company is backed by investors including Battery Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures, Sapphire, A‑Star, SV Angel and Homebrew Capital, and has support from notable tech leaders such as Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke and Dropbox co‑founders. Warp employs about 80 people and is headquartered in New York City.

_Usage:_

"How does Warp’s AI‑agent approach differ from using separate payroll or HR SaaS tools?"

"Warp consolidates payroll, HR, compliance, benefits and IT into one platform and uses AI agents to automate the tasks that traditional SaaS tools leave for manual handling, so companies can cut admin overhead without stitching together multiple products."

nodes.title: rex.fit
nodes.description: Rex.Fit offers an AI-powered wearable camera that automates nutrition tracking. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.rex.fit | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rex-fit

Rex.Fit’s DROP is an AI wearable camera that uses computer‑vision to automatically track users’ nutrition and provide recommendations. Since its launch last month the device has secured more than $93 k in pre‑orders, roughly 450 units, demonstrating early consumer interest. The underlying nutrition‑estimation technology is also offered as an API to fitness chains, which have reported hundreds of thousands of dollars in annual revenue from its use. The product is built by two brothers who are sports nutritionists and computer‑vision engineers from ETH Zurich, and the company operates out of San Francisco with a two‑person team.

_Usage:_

"How does DROP’s computer‑vision nutrition tracking compare to manually logging meals in a food diary?"

"DROP captures images of food and applies its computer‑vision model to estimate nutritional content, eliminating the need for users to manually enter each item. While the exact accuracy isn’t disclosed, the fact that fitness chains have integrated the API and generated significant revenue suggests it provides a usable level of estimation for real‑world fitness applications."

nodes.title: Stralis Aircraft
nodes.description: Stralis Aircraft builds emission‑free hydrogen electric aircraft. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://stralis.aero/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/stralis-aircraft

Stralis Aircraft designs and manufactures hydrogen‑electric airplanes that fly ten times farther than comparable battery‑electric models while offering lower operating costs than conventional fossil‑fuel aircraft. Its first product is a fifteen‑seat aircraft with an 800 km range slated to enter service in 2026 with launch customer Skytrans. The company’s team of four in Brisbane brings over 85 years of aerospace experience, having developed, flight‑tested and certified aircraft at organisations such as Google X, magniX, Heart Aerospace, Ampaire, Airbus, Boeing, Bombardier and Gulfstream. Stralis Aircraft has secured $145 million in letters of intent from seven airlines across the United States, Europe and Australia, underscoring market interest in its zero‑emission solution.

_Usage:_

"How does Stralis achieve a range ten times longer than battery‑electric aircraft?"

"Stralis uses hydrogen fuel‑cell technology to generate electricity for propulsion, which provides a much higher energy‑density than batteries; this allows its aircraft to travel farther on a single refuel while remaining emission‑free and keeping operating costs below those of fossil‑fuel planes."

nodes.title: Airbyte
nodes.description: Airbyte provides a context layer that AI agents query before acting, cutting tool calls and token usage. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://airbyte.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/airbyte

Airbyte Agents is the context layer that AI agents query before they act. It features the Context Store, which unifies entities across Salesforce, Stripe, Zendesk and more, and can be used from the UI, an LLM via MCP, or the SDK. The system achieves 40% fewer tool calls and up to 80% fewer tokens.

Airbyte Data Replication is the leading open data movement platform that empowers data teams in the AI era by transforming raw data into actionable intelligence. With a team of 90 engineers based in San Francisco, the company focuses on B2B data engineering and developer tools.

_Usage:_

"How does Airbyte's Context Store reduce token usage compared to traditional agent pipelines?"

"Airbyte's Context Store unifies data from platforms such as Salesforce, Stripe, and Zendesk, letting agents query context directly. This reduces the need for repeated external tool calls, cutting tool calls by 40% and token usage by up to 80% compared to pipelines that fetch context via separate calls."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.fountain9.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fountain9

Fountain9 is a predictive inventory planning solution that helps food brands and retailers reduce waste and improve product availability by forecasting future inventory needs. It uses a demand sensing and pricing engine that incorporates historical sales trends, seasonality, holidays, markdown events, and pricing changes to predict demand and optimize prices.

The platform aligns predicted demand with supply-side data to identify ideal suppliers and replenishment quantities, minimizing stock outs and waste. Fountain9 was acquired.

"Fountain9’s engine incorporates multiple real‑time factors—seasonality, holidays, markdown events, and pricing changes—to forecast demand and optimize prices, then aligns those predictions with supply‑side data to recommend suppliers and replenishment quantities, a step beyond conventional static forecasting."

nodes.title: Stacksi
nodes.description: Automates the completion of enterprise security questionnaires to accelerate deal closure. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.stacksi.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/stacksi

Stacksi enables fast-growing enterprise startups to automate the process of answering security questionnaires, freeing up engineering time for strategic projects. By allowing sales teams and executives to upload existing security policies and incoming questionnaires, the platform parses these documents to identify gaps against industry standards and helps establish a robust security program. This approach allows companies to quickly navigate enterprise security audits and improve their overall security posture while closing deals faster.

The company, which operated with a small remote team based in Los Angeles, was acquired, marking a significant milestone for this B2B security tool.

_Usage:_

"How does Stacksi handle the initial setup for a company that already has written security policies?"

"You upload your existing written security policies along with the new security questionnaire into the system. Stacksi then parses both sets of documents to identify any gaps between your current policies and the standards required by the questionnaire, helping you automate the completion process and address those gaps."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://soundry.ai/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/soundry-ai

Soundry AI builds generative AI tools that enhance fan engagement by allowing listeners to remix songs into any musical style. Its flagship product, Groove, can transform a track like Taylor Swift into the heavy‑metal style of Slayer, demonstrating the platform’s flexibility.

"Groove lets users specify both the source track and a target genre, producing a remix that matches the chosen style—e.g., turning a pop song into a metal version—whereas many generic AI music tools only generate new compositions without a direct style‑transfer capability."

Quadrant Eye is a San Francisco-based startup that set out to make eye exams fully online, enabling patients to get high-quality care from their homes. It aimed to improve eyecare access and fight preventable blindness.

nodes.title: Kivo Health
nodes.description: Kivo Health delivers AI-powered virtual care for seniors with chronic disease, starting with lung care. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://kivohealth.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/kivo-health

Kivo Health provides AI-powered virtual care aimed at seniors managing chronic disease, initially focusing on lung health. The platform keeps patients out of the hospital and saves payers more than $8,000 per patient on average. It partners with major health systems such as Stanford, UCLA and Optum Health, and recently closed a $10 million Series A round while scaling its 40‑person team in San Francisco.

The company’s AI-driven approach targets cost reduction and improved outcomes in the senior population, positioning it as a notable player in digital health and telehealth services.

_Usage:_

"How does Kivo Health’s AI virtual care differ from standard telehealth services?"

"Kivo Health’s solution combines AI-driven monitoring and decision support specifically for seniors with chronic disease, starting with lung care, whereas typical telehealth platforms offer general video visits without that disease‑focused AI layer. This specialization helps keep patients out of the hospital and generates average savings of over $8,000 per patient for payers."

nodes.title: Mindbase
nodes.description: Mindbase creates autonomous AI influencers that generate content and engage fans on social platforms. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mymindbase.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/tradex

Mindbase is an AI avatar platform that launches digital personas, both based on real humans and entirely artificial, to operate as influencers on Instagram and YouTube. The company equips each AI influencer with dedicated communication channels, including email, phone numbers, and WhatsApp accounts, to facilitate deep relationship building with audiences similar to human creators. The platform currently generates over 5 million daily views through a network of more than 10 AI influencers.

The business model involves brands paying monthly fees for access to these AI influencers, with reported costs ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per month per entity. Mindbase cites a case where a brand partner achieved a 15x return on ad spend, generating $45,000 in sales from a $3,000 investment. The company projects that generating $20,000 annually per influencer could scale the business to $100 million in annual recurring revenue with a network of 5,000 entities.

Based in San Francisco and operating remotely, the seven-person team consists of IIT alumni and repeat founders. They previously built TradeX, a prediction market platform that reached $40 million in monthly trading volume with 5 million users, leveraging trend tracking and influencer partnership expertise that they are now applying to the AI influencer space.

_Usage:_

"How does Mindbase differentiate its AI influencers from standard chatbots or static virtual avatars?"

"Unlike static avatars or simple chatbots, Mindbase assigns each AI influencer a full suite of communication tools, including a unique email address, phone number, and WhatsApp account. This allows the digital persona to engage in multi-channel, persistent interactions that mimic the depth of relationships formed with human creators, rather than just posting content."

Reality Defender is the market leader in deepfake detection, offering real‑time protection for enterprises and governments against deepfake and agentic fraud. "Reality Defender’s platform continuously scans incoming media streams, using AI models trained on synthetic and real content to flag deepfakes instantly, whereas traditional forensic methods typically analyze static footage after the fact."

nodes.title: Karate Labs
nodes.description: Open-source platform for unified API and UI test automation. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://karatelabs.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/karate-labs

Karate Labs provides an open-source unified test automation platform that combines API testing, performance testing, API mocking, and UI testing. The tool is designed to reduce friction in the developer experience by allowing users to write tests with low code, simulate end-user workflows, and reuse API tests for performance validation.

The platform emphasizes a local-first approach, ensuring that user data remains within the customer's firewall for security. Karate has achieved significant adoption with 1.5 million monthly downloads and usage by over 500 companies, including 76 of the Fortune 500. The company offers official plugins for IntelliJ and VS Code to simplify installation, configuration, and maintenance, while also providing premium features such as async API testing and API documentation.

_Usage:_

"How does Karate handle data privacy compared to cloud-based testing tools?"

"Karate follows a local-first approach where user data stays within the customer's firewall, addressing security concerns often associated with cloud-based solutions. It integrates via official IntelliJ and VS Code plugins to simplify onboarding and maintenance while keeping the core testing logic local."

nodes.title: Emobi
nodes.description: A unified legal, financial, and technical infrastructure for secure and automated EV charging across North America. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.emobi.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/emobi

Emobi provides a single point of integration for electric vehicle charging, combining legal, financial, and technical infrastructure to power apps, fleets, and automakers. Its core technology, JustPlug, enables fully automated and secure charging that works instantly with existing hardware, requiring no special software or setup.

The company has integrated over 122,000 EV chargers across the U.S. and Canada, positioning it as the largest EV charging ecosystem in North America. Emobi serves more than 15 enterprise customers and is trusted by the U.S. Department of Energy and the Department of Transportation.

Headquartered in San Francisco, the nine-person team holds two provisional patents and focuses on maximizing charger utilization through its API-driven platform.

_Usage:_

"How does Emobi's JustPlug technology handle the complexity of connecting to different charging networks without requiring new hardware?"

"JustPlug acts as a unified layer that abstracts the legal, financial, and technical differences between various EV charging networks. Instead of requiring drivers or fleet managers to manage multiple accounts or install specific software, it allows for instant, secure, and automated charging sessions using existing infrastructure, effectively standardizing the experience across the 122,000+ chargers in its ecosystem."

nodes.title: Yezza
nodes.description: Storefronts on WhatsApp for small businesses in Southeast Asia. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://yezza.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/yezza

Yezza enables small businesses in Southeast Asia to create and manage storefronts directly within WhatsApp. The platform supports various commerce use cases beyond simple product sales, including social media influencer collaborations and table reservations. Yezza is based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, and operates as a B2B SaaS provider.

The company emerged from a previous tech-enabled travel business that utilized WhatsApp to sell packages, which was spun off during the pandemic. Yezza has achieved profitability with a monthly recurring revenue of $40K and generates $3M in monthly GMV from approximately 1,500 daily orders. Merchants pay a monthly fee starting at $12 plus up to $0.25 per order.

Yezza targets a market estimated at $7.2B, driven by 50M WhatsApp Business downloads in the region. The company is backed by Y Combinator and angels with experience at Facebook and WhatsApp, and it notes that similar buying behaviors via WhatsApp exist in Latin America and Africa.

_Usage:_

"How does Yezza handle the logistics of selling physical goods if the entire transaction happens inside WhatsApp?"

"Yezza acts as the storefront layer within the WhatsApp interface, allowing merchants to list products and process orders without forcing customers to leave the chat app. It handles the e-commerce mechanics like order tracking and payment collection, charging merchants a monthly subscription and a small per-order fee, while leveraging the existing user base of WhatsApp Business in Southeast Asia."

nodes.title: Perl Street
nodes.description: Democratizing structured finance to unlock capital for sustainable infrastructure and next-generation hardware. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://perlstreet.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/perl-street

Perl Street operates a platform designed to democratize structured finance, specifically targeting the financing needs of sustainable infrastructure and next-generation hardware technologies. The company addresses the massive capital gap required for climate action, noting that reaching net zero emissions requires over $4 trillion per year in global clean energy investment according to IEA estimates.

By facilitating debt financing, Perl Street has helped multiple hardware startups secure over $140M in offers from reputable institutions. The platform focuses on upgrading critical physical assets such as energy storage devices, electric vehicles, charging stations, and building electrification systems.

The company is based in Sydney, Austin, and remote locations, with a small team of four. It operates within the fintech and credit sectors, emphasizing that the future of distributed and resilient infrastructure is dependent on accessible financing for new hardware.

_Usage:_

"How does Perl Street actually get hardware startups the debt financing they need when traditional banks might be hesitant about new tech?"

"Perl Street acts as a platform that structures these deals to make them accessible to reputable financial institutions, effectively unlocking capital for projects that might otherwise struggle to find traditional debt financing. They have already facilitated over $140M in debt offers for hardware startups, focusing on areas like energy storage and EV infrastructure where the capital requirements are high but the technology is essential for climate goals."

nodes.description: AI and human-powered automation for operations and workflows. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.lumibot.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/lumina

Lumina is a job platform based in Singapore that connects 1.5 million workers with 30,000 companies in Southeast Asia. The company has expanded its services globally through Lumibot, a bespoke automation service that combines AI with human-in-the-loop support to handle repetitive business processes.

Lumibot targets use cases such as operations support, revenue operations, web and social media management, email handling, content moderation, and AI training. The service operates on a prepaid credit system with no minimum commitment, allowing businesses to automate complex workflows while maintaining flexibility through dedicated service managers and SLAs.

_Usage:_

"How does Lumina's pricing model work compared to traditional outsourcing agencies?"

"Lumina uses a prepaid credit system where AI-powered automation starts at $13 per hour, supplemented by human-in-the-loop support at $2 to $6 per hour. Unlike traditional agencies that often require long-term contracts, Lumina operates without minimum commitments and offers a fully refundable deposit starting at $500, providing more flexibility for businesses testing automation workflows."

nodes.title: Agave
nodes.description: AI financial operations platform for the construction industry. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.useagave.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/agave

Agave provides an AI-driven financial operations platform designed specifically for the construction sector, a $12 trillion global industry often reliant on legacy software built 20-40 years ago. The company addresses the fragmentation of this market by building infrastructure to read and write across on-premises systems that typically lack APIs or documentation.

Using these underlying rails, Agave deploys AI to automate critical financial tasks such as invoicing, expense management, compliance, and billing. The San Francisco-based company, which has a team of 40, has secured over 500 customers and has maintained profitability and positive cash flow for more than two years.

Backed by Accel and Y Combinator, with additional support from investors associated with Procore, Autodesk, and Plaid, Agave focuses on modernizing the financial backbone of construction businesses through specialized B2B SaaS solutions.

_Usage:_

"How does Agave handle the lack of APIs in legacy construction software?"

"They spent three years building custom rails to read and write directly across those older, on-prem systems, allowing them to deploy AI for financial tasks like invoicing and compliance without requiring the legacy software to have modern APIs or documentation."

nodes.title: Dataglade
nodes.description: Dataglade uses AI to generate clear analyses and financial models for any public company. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://dataglade.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dataglade

Dataglade provides AI‑generated analyses and financial models for public companies, drawing on a proprietary financial data warehouse that backs every number with citations. The service aims to eliminate the manual effort of digging through financial filings, saving investors hours each day. It informs over $1 billion of trades daily and serves customers who trust its reports for comprehensive research needs.

The company operates as a fintech SaaS platform out of New York City with a two‑person team. Since its Winter 2023 Y Combinator batch, Dataglade has positioned itself as a smart, AI‑driven alternative for stock research.

_Usage:_

"How does Dataglade’s AI‑generated research compare to using a traditional financial data platform?"

"Dataglade’s AI automatically writes analyses and builds financial models for any public company, and each figure is linked to citations from its own data warehouse, so users don’t have to manually extract numbers from filings. This contrasts with traditional platforms where analysts must pull data and craft reports themselves, which can be time‑consuming."

The company's mission is to become the primary data source for AI and API monetization, standardizing metering across B2B infrastructure. OpenMeter was acquired, reflecting the strategic value of its technology for larger players in the space.

This built-in standardization lets revenue and efficiency teams directly monetize AI and API consumption without building custom pipelines."

The project has earned over 50,000 stars on GitHub and is trusted by companies such as Rocket Money, Samsara, Lemonade, and Adobe. It is built for B2B use and is maintained by a 10-person team based in San Francisco.

"LiteLLM can call more than 100 LLM APIs, including Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, VertexAI, Cohere, and Anthropic, all through an OpenAI-compatible interface."

nodes.title: Pylon
nodes.description: An agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B companies to enable human-agent collaboration. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://usepylon.com/?utm_source=bookface&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=pylon-profile | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pylon-2

Pylon is an agentic support platform designed specifically for B2B enterprises, allowing human teams and AI agents to collaborate on customer work. The system investigates, resolves, and acts on signals across various channels, distinguishing itself from pre-AI platforms by enriching every interaction with deep account-level context.

By automating low-impact tasks and surfacing answers proactively, Pylon aims to accelerate response times and improve customer satisfaction while creating a self-improving support system. The company is headquartered in San Francisco with a team of 120 employees.

Pylon is used by hundreds of fast-growing YC companies, including Retool, Hightouch, and Deel, to manage their customer operations.

_Usage:_

"How does Pylon differ from traditional helpdesk tools that just added a chatbot?"

nodes.title: Inkeep
nodes.description: Build AI Agent teammates and automations in code or no-code. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://inkeep.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/inkeep

Inkeep is an agent platform designed to allow both developers and non-developers to ship AI-powered assistants and automations. The company provides a no-code builder and developer framework with full two-way sync, enabling teams to create agents that integrate with existing apps, APIs, and software via MCPs.

The platform offers unified search and RAG capabilities for knowledge bases, documentation, and company data, along with intelligent insights and monitoring for agent performance. Inkeep is used by companies such as Anthropic, Midjourney, Clay, PostHog, and Postman to deploy agents at scale for tasks ranging from support to sales.

Based in San Francisco, the 18-person team was backed by Khosla Ventures, Y-Combinator, and Great Point Ventures. It operates in the B2B space, focusing on engineering, product, and design workflows to help enterprises automate repeatable tasks.

_Usage:_

"How does Inkeep handle the gap between no-code builders and developer frameworks?"

"It provides a unified platform with full two-way sync between its no-code builder and developer framework, so changes made in one are reflected in the other. This allows non-developers to build agents visually while developers can extend or modify them in code, ensuring the same agent logic can be deployed across different teams without manual re-implementation."

nodes.title: Storyboarder
nodes.description: A tool and platform for creating, sharing, and selling webcomics using 3D and AI. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://storyboarder.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/storyboarder

Storyboarder is a Y Combinator W23 company that provides a tool and platform for anyone to create, share, and sell webcomics. The company aims to address the limitations of the existing webcomic market, where content variety is constrained by the need for creators to possess drawing skills, despite high reader demand for diverse stories.

Leveraging years of experience building storyboarding software for filmmakers, which has reached 700K users, Storyboarder is developing next-generation tools that utilize video game interfaces, ubiquitous 3D compute, and AI. This approach allows users to easily create scenes and pose characters, effectively democratizing visual storytelling for a broader audience.

The company is based in New York City and operates remotely with a small team of two. It is backed by Y Combinator, David Karp, Andrew Kortina, and other product-focused investors.

_Usage:_

"How does this differ from traditional digital art tools for comics?"

"Unlike traditional tools that require users to draw from scratch, Storyboarder uses 3D compute and AI to let users create scenes and pose characters without needing drawing skills, similar to how video game interfaces work."

nodes.title: Fairway Health
nodes.description: Fairway Health provides an AI co‑pilot that helps health insurers quickly authorize patient treatments. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.fairwayhealth.co/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fairway-health

Fairway Health offers an AI‑assistant that speeds up the authorization of patient treatments for health insurers. The system uses large language models to analyze long, messy medical records—often over 70 pages—and determine whether a patient is eligible for a specific treatment. By automating this analysis, insurers can process authorizations faster than manual review.

The company was acquired, reflecting the market’s interest in AI‑driven health‑insurance workflow automation. Fairway Health operates with a small team of three people across New York City, Philadelphia, Boston, and remote locations, focusing on the healthcare and healthcare‑IT sectors.

_Usage:_

"How does Fairway Health’s AI co‑pilot handle 70‑page medical records compared to a traditional manual review process?"

"It runs a large language model over the full record to extract relevant clinical details and eligibility criteria, producing a decision recommendation without a human having to read every page, which speeds up the authorization workflow."

nodes.title: Flower
nodes.description: An open-source framework for training AI models on distributed data using federated learning. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://flower.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/flower

Flower Labs provides Flower, an open-source framework and ecosystem designed for training artificial intelligence on distributed data and compute resources. The platform utilizes federated learning to allow organizations to improve their AI models on sensitive data that remains securely distributed across organizational silos or user devices, rather than being centralized.

The company argues that most current AI relies on centralized public datasets, which represent only a fraction of available data. By unlocking access to private data, Flower aims to drive the next breakthroughs in artificial intelligence while maintaining privacy and collaboration.

Flower Labs is a Y Combinator W23 graduate with a remote team of 20. It is trusted by industry leaders including Mozilla, Banking Circle, Samsung, Temenos, and Bosch, and is backed by investors such as Felicis, First Spark Ventures, and Mozilla Ventures.

_Usage:_

"How does Flower handle data privacy compared to standard centralized training pipelines?"

"Flower uses federated learning to keep sensitive data distributed across organizational silos or user devices instead of aggregating it in a central location. This allows models to be trained on private data without exposing the underlying information, which is particularly useful for industries like banking or healthcare where data cannot be centralized due to security or regulatory constraints."

nodes.title: Persana AI
nodes.description: Autonomous AI agents that research, enrich, and engage prospects using 100+ data sources to boost sales pipeline. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.persana.ai/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/persana-ai

Persana AI provides an agent layer for modern go-to-market teams, replacing fragmented point solutions with a unified platform that autonomously researches, enriches, and engages prospects. The system utilizes a multi-agent architecture to track funding, hiring, and tech changes across over 100 data sources, executing complex workflows without manual triggers or platform limits.

Trained on 700 million contacts and 200 million companies, Persana employs proprietary embeddings fine-tuned for GTM use cases to continuously learn which actions convert to pipeline. It features bi-directional native integration with major CRMs like Salesforce and HubSpot, allowing teams to scale prospecting without adding headcount while reclaiming time previously spent on manual work.

Founded by LinkedIn engineering veterans and backed by Y Combinator, Persana AI was acquired, marking its exit from the YC Winter 2023 batch.

_Usage:_

"How does Persana handle prospecting differently than standard workflow automation tools?"

"Instead of relying on predefined rules and manual triggers, Persana uses autonomous agents that think, learn, and execute 24/7. It consolidates data from over 100 sources into a single agentic platform, allowing it to run complex workflows across large prospect lists without the hard limits or fragmentation typical of traditional workflow tools."

nodes.title: Fern
nodes.description: Generates SDKs and API documentation from a single source of truth. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.buildwithfern.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fern

Fern solves the common pain points of API development by generating SDKs and API documentation that are typed, standardized, and always in sync. The platform allows companies to maintain a single source of truth, eliminating the drift that often occurs across multiple documentation and codebases.

Since launching in Winter 2023, the Brooklyn-based team of fewer than 40 engineers has built an open-source tool trusted by over 200 customers. Notable users include Square, Webflow, ElevenLabs, Auth0, and Intercom, who use Fern to power their developer and agent experiences. Fern was acquired, marking a significant milestone for the developer tools space.

_Usage:_

"How does Fern handle the synchronization between code and documentation compared to manual updates?"

"Fern generates both the SDKs and the API docs from a single source of truth, which ensures they are always in sync and typed. This removes the need for manual updates across different files, addressing the issue of unstandardized and out-of-sync APIs that often plague traditional development workflows."
