nodes.title: DAGWorks Inc.
nodes.description: Open source tools for building reliable AI agents and applications with integrated observability. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.dagworks.io/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dagworks-inc

DAGWorks provides open source frameworks and services designed to make AI agents and applications more reliable by standardizing how Python code expresses data, ML, LLM, and agent workflows. The company was acquired, marking a significant milestone for its developer-focused infrastructure. Its platform emphasizes an integrated development and observability experience that allows teams to collaborate and connect their AI systems more effectively.

The company operates two primary open source projects: Burr, which focuses on AI applications, and Hamilton, which handles AI pipelines and workflows. Both projects include self-hostable UIs as well as enterprise and SaaS offerings. By requiring only a one-line code change, developers can gain versioning, lineage, tracing, cataloging, and observability features out of the box, which helps reduce total cost of ownership and speeds up time to production.

_Usage:_

"How does DAGWorks handle observability for AI pipelines compared to building custom logging?"

"DAGWorks uses lightweight frameworks like Hamilton and Burr that integrate observability directly into the code structure. Instead of building custom logging, you add a single line of code to enable versioning, lineage, tracing, and cataloging automatically. This approach standardizes how workflows are expressed in Python, making it easier to maintain and monitor AI systems without significant overhead."

nodes.title: Helicone
nodes.description: Helicone provides an open-source observability platform for monitoring, debugging, and optimizing LLM applications. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.helicone.ai/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/helicone

Helicone is a developer-focused observability platform designed to simplify the operational aspects of deploying Large Language Models. Based in San Francisco, the company offers a unified view of performance, cost, and user interaction metrics across various LLM providers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and LangChain. By centralizing logs and metrics, it allows engineers to track costs, understand user interactions, and optimize outputs from a single interface.

The platform supports advanced features such as prompt management, performance tracing, and debugging, enabling teams to experiment with prompts and track success rates to improve response quality. Helicone also addresses data privacy concerns by offering deployment options for dedicated instances, hybrid cloud integrations, or self-hosted environments, giving clients control over their data while ensuring compliance with privacy standards.

As a YC Winter 2023 company, Helicone has been acquired, marking a significant milestone in the growing market for AI infrastructure tools. Its focus on providing transparency and control for engineers and data scientists has positioned it as a key tool for teams scaling AI applications.

_Usage:_

"How does Helicone handle data privacy for companies that can't send their LLM logs to a public cloud?"

"Helicone supports flexible deployment options, including dedicated instances, hybrid cloud integrations, or fully self-hosted environments. This allows teams to maintain control over their data and ensure compliance with privacy standards without sacrificing the observability features."

nodes.title: Artifact
nodes.description: Artifact offers a collaborative AI-native IDE that accelerates every stage of hardware engineering. YC W25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.artifact.engineer/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/artifact-2

Artifact is a collaborative integrated development environment built specifically for hardware engineers. It connects the full engineering lifecycle—from design and procurement through manufacturing, integration, test, and sustainment—within a single UI. The platform includes an AI copilot that automatically generates and verifies design artifacts, linking each output to a single source of truth. Artifact’s approach is intended to make hardware development more rigorous, deliberate, and system‑aware, and the company works directly with customers tackling complex technical problems. Artifact has raised $3.5 million and operates with a four‑person team in Los Angeles. The startup is part of Y Combinator’s Winter 2025 batch and remains active.

_Usage:_

"How does Artifact’s AI copilot differ from the AI features in standard CAD tools?"

"Artifact’s copilot automatically generates every engineering artifact and ties it to a single source of truth across the entire hardware lifecycle, rather than just offering design suggestions within a CAD interface. This end‑to‑end traceability and integration across procurement, manufacturing, and test is what sets it apart."

nodes.title: Traceloop
nodes.description: Provides OpenTelemetry-based observability for LLM applications to track prompts, responses, and failures. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.traceloop.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/traceloop

Traceloop offers full visibility into Large Language Model (LLM) operations by tracking every prompt, response, and failure. The platform allows developers to monitor quality, detect drift, and prevent hallucinations from reaching end users. It is powered by OpenTelemetry and integrates into existing stacks with a single line of code.

Founded in Winter 2023, the company operates as a B2B SaaS provider with a team of nine based in Tel Aviv, Israel. Traceloop was acquired, marking its exit from the independent startup phase.

_Usage:_

"How does Traceloop handle observability for LLM apps compared to standard APM tools?"

"It leverages OpenTelemetry to provide specific visibility into LLM interactions, such as prompts and responses, rather than just general application metrics. This allows you to track quality and detect drift or hallucinations directly within the LLM workflow, integrating via a single line of code."

nodes.title: StackAI
nodes.description: Deploys custom AI agents to automate complex enterprise back-office workflows. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.stackai.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/stackai

StackAI is an enterprise AI transformation platform that partners with large organizations to deploy custom AI agents for automating complex back-office workflows. The company provides a no-code interface that allows teams to build and manage agents handling tasks such as compliance audits, legal intake, due diligence research, and insurance claim underwriting.

Notable clients include BAE Systems, Monzo, Morgan & Morgan, and Goodwill, which use the platform to integrate AI into their core operations. With a team of 62 based in San Francisco, StackAI focuses on the B2B sector, specifically targeting high-stakes operational processes that require precision and scale.

The company was acquired by Asana in May 2026, marking a significant consolidation in the enterprise AI agent space.

_Usage:_

"How does StackAI handle complex, multi-step back-office tasks like compliance audits without requiring engineering resources?"

"StackAI uses a no-code platform to let business teams define and deploy custom AI agents that can execute multi-step workflows. Instead of writing code, users configure agents to handle specific tasks like legal intake or due diligence, allowing the system to automate these processes directly within existing enterprise operations."

nodes.title: Onlook
nodes.description: An open-source visual editor for code that merges design, development, and AI to accelerate web app creation. YC W25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://onlook.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/onlook

Onlook is a San Francisco-based developer tool that functions as a visual editor for code, aiming to close the gap between design and development. The platform allows users to build, deploy, and iterate on websites and web apps by integrating AI capabilities directly into the workflow.

The project gained significant traction shortly after launch, reaching the top of Hacker News and becoming the number one trending repository on GitHub, surpassing DeepSeek in popularity. It has accumulated over 8,500 GitHub stars, reflecting strong interest in its approach to merging design and development.

Founded by Daniel Farrell and Kiet Ho, the four-person team combines design expertise with engineering backgrounds from Amazon and ServiceNow. Onlook positions itself as a comprehensive solution for anyone looking to streamline the process of creating and maintaining web applications.

_Usage:_

"How does Onlook differ from traditional low-code platforms or standard IDEs?"

"Onlook acts as a visual editor for code rather than a black-box generator, allowing designers and developers to work in the same environment. Unlike standard IDEs that are purely text-based, it integrates AI to help bridge the gap between design intent and actual code, enabling faster iteration on web apps without losing control over the underlying implementation."

Revi helps investment banks, private equity firms, and corporate development teams source new M&A deals by automating the end‑to‑end origination workflow. It uses agentic AI workflows that replicate the full deal‑sourcing process, eliminating the usual trade‑off between precision and scalability.

The company launched its first version in September 2023 and is already used by KPMG and platforms backed by KKR and Nordic Capital. With a small team of two operating from New York City and remotely, Revi targets B2B sales functions in the finance sector.

"Revi’s agentic workflow automates the entire deal‑origination pipeline rather than just providing a list of leads, so it can maintain the same precision of a manual process while scaling to handle many opportunities at once, which typical sourcing tools don’t achieve."

nodes.title: ZeroEntropy
nodes.description: Trains small, task-specific models to replace frontier LLMs on specialized production AI workloads. YC W25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.zeroentropy.dev | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/zeroentropy

ZeroEntropy trains small, task-specific models designed to replace frontier LLMs across production AI pipelines. Most AI applications rely on general-purpose models for narrow, repeatable pipeline steps like reranking, embedding, classification, routing, query rewriting, and context compression. Running these discrete tasks on frontier models creates unnecessary latency and high operating costs.

By focusing on specialized models for these intermediate workloads, the platform helps developers deploy AI systems that run faster, cheaper, and more accurately. Based in San Francisco, ZeroEntropy participated in the Y Combinator Winter 2025 batch with a team of six.

ZeroEntropy has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"Why swap out a frontier LLM for task-specific models in an AI pipeline?"

"Frontier LLMs are often overkill for narrow, repeatable steps like routing, classification, context compression, or reranking. Relying on general-purpose models for every stage of a pipeline makes production AI slow and expensive, whereas small task-specific models handle those specific workloads faster, cheaper, and more accurately."

nodes.title: Scale AI
nodes.description: Scale provides data‑centric infrastructure that accelerates AI development. YC S16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://scale.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/scale-ai

Scale provides data‑centric infrastructure that accelerates AI development in organizations of any size, delivering critical business insights and operational efficiency.

The platform leverages Reinforced Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) to help companies build the strongest AI models that supercharge their operations.

Scale’s customer base spans major tech firms, defense agencies, automotive research institutes, and fintech and logistics companies, including Meta, Microsoft, the U.S. Army, the DoD’s Defense Innovation Unit, OpenAI, General Motors, Toyota Research Institute, Brex, Instacart, and Flexport. With a team of 500 employees based in San Francisco, the company has positioned itself as a key player in AI infrastructure.

_Usage:_

"How does Scale's RLHF approach differ from traditional supervised learning?"

"Scale’s RLHF uses human feedback to iteratively refine model outputs, enabling stronger AI models for business tasks compared to standard supervised learning that relies solely on labeled data."

nodes.title: Expo
nodes.description: Expo provides a unified toolchain for building cross-platform mobile and web apps with JavaScript. YC S16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://expo.dev | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/expo

Expo enables developers to write applications in JavaScript that run natively on Android, iOS, and the web. By combining the rapid iteration cycles and easy deployment of web development with the performance and device capabilities of native apps, it simplifies the mobile development process.

The platform includes Expo Application Services (EAS), a suite of cloud services designed to accelerate the release of Expo and React Native apps to app stores. These services help teams grow by streamlining the path from code to production.

Founded in the Summer 2016 batch, the company operates out of San Francisco and Palo Alto with a team of 40 engineers focused on B2B developer infrastructure.

_Usage:_

"How does Expo compare to using raw React Native for cross-platform development?"

"Expo wraps React Native with a managed workflow that adds automatic cross-platform support, fast iteration cycles, and easy deploys. It also includes Expo Application Services (EAS) to handle the complexities of getting apps to the stores, effectively reducing the friction of native app distribution compared to managing those processes manually."

nodes.body:

nodes.title: Within
nodes.description: Within maps enterprise workflows to structure work and reallocate tasks between humans and AI agents. YC S18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://within.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/within

Within, formerly known as Klarity, operates as a Company Brain designed to help organizations manage the transition to AI-driven operations. The platform is used by major enterprises including OpenAI, DoorDash, ServiceNow, Salesforce, JLL, and McKesson to facilitate AI transformation by mapping how work is actually performed.

The product functions through a web-based application that requires no installation, allowing employees to share their screens while working normally. Within captures and anonymizes every task, sending signals back to users to highlight their strengths. These individual activities are then consolidated by Within agents into a comprehensive enterprise map that details decision-making processes, approval flows, and control enforcement.

Based on this structural data, the company identifies opportunities to deploy AI agents against specific business objectives. It builds these agents and redesigns the surrounding people, processes, and rituals to ensure harmonious collaboration between human employees and automated systems.

_Usage:_

"How does Within capture workflow data without disrupting employee productivity or requiring heavy IT deployment?"

"It uses a lightweight web app where employees simply log in and share their screens while working as usual. The system maps and anonymizes tasks in real-time to build a structural model of the enterprise, eliminating the need for software installations or manual process documentation."

nodes.title: Dialect
nodes.description: Dialect builds blockchain links that let businesses unbundle product experiences from apps for instant, no‑redirect actions. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://dialect.to | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dialect

Dialect is on a mission to organize the internet’s experiences and make them distributable and actionable everywhere. It uses blockchain links, called blinks, a new technology that lets businesses unbundle their product experiences from their apps and sites.

The blinks enable users to take instant, no‑redirect actions wherever they are. This technology is unique to blockchain today and is positioned to redefine how we interact with the internet as the world moves on‑chain.

Dialect was acquired after its Summer 2020 batch. The B2B crypto/Web3 startup is based in New York City and employs eight people.

_Usage:_

"How do Dialect’s blinks differ from traditional deep links?"

"Dialect’s blinks are blockchain‑based links that let a business separate its product experience from any specific app or website, so a user can act instantly without a redirect. Traditional deep links rely on the target app being installed and typically route through the app, whereas blinks work on‑chain and avoid those redirects."

nodes.title: REVER
nodes.description: A global platform that enables two-click returns and 24-hour refunds for e-commerce. YC S22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://itsrever.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/rever

REVER is a Barcelona-based fintech and logistics company that simplifies the post-sale experience in e-commerce. The platform allows shoppers to initiate returns in just two clicks and receive refunds within 24 hours, aiming to make returning items as easy as buying them. By handling over 100 million euros in yearly returns, REVER positions itself as a comprehensive solution for global online returns.

The company operates with a team of 35 people and generates more than 50 million euros in annual revenue. Its infrastructure supports frictionless and sustainable returns for merchants, addressing the logistical and financial complexities typically associated with product returns. REVER’s model focuses on reducing friction for consumers while providing a scalable backend for e-commerce businesses.

_Usage:_

"How does REVER handle the logistics and financial risk of instant refunds?"

"REVER acts as a global platform that manages the entire post-sale process, allowing merchants to offer two-click returns and 24-hour refunds. It handles over 100 million euros in annual returns, effectively absorbing the logistical and financial complexity of processing these transactions so that the checkout and return experience remains seamless for the end user."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://emergent.sh | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/emergent

Emergent builds autonomous coding agents that replace traditional software development by generating, testing, and deploying production applications directly from plain-language intent. Its systems run in production at global scale and are used to build millions of real applications.
Since its public launch, Emergent has reached $50M ARR in seven months, making it one of the fastest‑growing startups. More than five million users in over 190 countries have built six million applications on the platform, and it has raised $100M from investors including Khosla Ventures, SoftBank, Google, Lightspeed India, Prosus Ventures, Together Fund, and Y Combinator.

_Usage:_

"Is Emergent just another no‑code builder, or does it actually write code?"

"Emergent’s platform uses autonomous coding agents that generate, test, and deploy production‑grade code from plain-language prompts, so it creates real applications rather than just assembling drag‑and‑drop components."

nodes.title: KERNEL
nodes.description: Open source infrastructure enabling AI agents to access the internet with sub-150ms cold starts. YC S25.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.kernel.sh | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/kernel

Kernel provides open source infrastructure that allows AI agents to interact with the web at high speed. By leveraging unikernels, the platform achieves sub-150ms cold starts for managed headful browsers while maintaining low resource usage. This architecture supports persistent sessions that retain cookies and authentication across invocations, ensuring continuity for agent workflows.

The system includes built-in stealth capabilities such as residential proxies and automatic CAPTCHA solving, alongside full observability features like session recording and live views. Kernel is designed to integrate natively with existing browser and computer use frameworks, offering a SOC 2 compliant and HIPAA-ready environment for enterprise deployment.

Trusted by over 1,000 organizations including Cash App and Rye, Kernel is backed by Accel and Y Combinator. The company operates out of San Francisco with a team of six engineers focused on building robust cloud infrastructure for the emerging agent economy.

_Usage:_

"How does Kernel handle the latency and stealth requirements for AI agents browsing the web?"

"Kernel uses unikernels to keep cold starts under 150ms, which is critical for real-time agent interactions. It also handles the messy parts of web access by including residential proxies and automatic CAPTCHA solving out of the box, so agents don't get blocked, while maintaining persistent sessions to keep authentication state intact between calls."

nodes.title: Manicule

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://manicule.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/manicule

It owns developer documentation and technical content across social channels end-to-end. _Usage:_

"How does Manicule differ from traditional SEO tools for AI agents?"

"Manicule provides a full DevRel service that owns documentation and technical content across channels, whereas traditional SEO/GEO SaaS tools only show ranking data and lack agent expertise."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://theathletic.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/the-athletic

The Athletic is a subscription-based digital sports media company that produces in-depth articles, podcasts, and premium video content. nodes.title: Flutterwave
nodes.description: Building payments infrastructure to connect businesses across Africa to the global economy. YC S16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://flutterwave.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/flutterwave

Flutterwave provides technology, tools, and infrastructure for businesses and banks seeking to offer seamless and secure payment experiences. Founded in 2016, the company aims to build the necessary payment rails to integrate African markets into the broader global financial system.

The company has grown to become one of the fastest-growing payments firms in the world, operating across more than 33 African countries. Since its inception, Flutterwave has processed close to $20 billion in payments and 100 million transactions, supported by a team of 500 employees based in Lagos and Los Angeles.

Flutterwave has attracted significant investment from experienced fintech investors, including Y Combinator Continuity Fund, Greycroft, and the Omidyar Network. In 2017, it was named Africa’s best fintech company at the Apps Africa Innovation Awards.

_Usage:_

"How does Flutterwave differ from global payment processors like Stripe in terms of regional coverage?"

"Flutterwave focuses specifically on enabling businesses to make and accept payments across 33 African countries, providing the local infrastructure needed to connect these markets to the global economy. While global players like Stripe offer broad international coverage, Flutterwave is notable for its deep integration and scale within the African region, having processed nearly $20 billion in transactions since 2016."

nodes.title: Pursuit
nodes.description: Enabling Twitch streamers to engage and monetize their fan bases through recognition and interaction tools. YC S16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.revlo.co | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pursuit

Pursuit, operating under the brand Revlo, helped eSports streamers on Twitch better connect with and monetize their fan bases. The company addressed the limitation of standard IRC chat rooms by allowing streamers to reward loyal fans with recognition, merchandise, and direct interaction opportunities. This approach aimed to drive higher repeat viewership and conversion into paid subscriptions for streamers.

The startup was based in San Francisco and focused on the consumer gaming sector, specifically within the creator economy. Pursuit was acquired, marking the end of its independent operations.

"Standard Twitch interaction relied heavily on cluttered IRC chat rooms, which limited direct engagement. Revlo provided tools for streamers to actively reward fans with recognition, merchandise, and specific interaction opportunities, turning passive viewers into more engaged subscribers."

Burrow was named one of the 10 most innovative retail brands in the world by Fast Company in 2018, and its sofa was recognized as one of the 50 best inventions of the year by TIME.

"Burrow ships its products within a week, leveraging a design that allows items to assemble and disassemble easily. This modular approach likely reduces shipping complexity and costs compared to traditional bulky furniture, making it a more efficient direct-to-consumer model."

nodes.title: SimpleCitizen
nodes.description: Simplifies the US citizenship application process with an online questionnaire. YC S16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.simplecitizen.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/simplecitizen

SimpleCitizen streamlines the complex process of applying for US citizenship by guiding applicants through a streamlined online experience. The platform allows users to answer just 20 questions in approximately 20 minutes, aiming to make the procedure as straightforward as filling out a job application. By automating this step, the service helps users avoid significant legal fees associated with traditional application methods.

Based in Salt Lake City, Utah, the company operated with a team of 23 people before being acquired. It focused on the consumer and civic tech sectors, specifically targeting individuals navigating the US immigration system. The acquisition marks the end of its independent operation, consolidating its approach to simplifying government-related applications.

_Usage:_

"How does SimpleCitizen replace the need for a lawyer in the citizenship process?"

"It replaces the initial intake and form-filling phase by using a 20-question online survey that takes about 20 minutes to complete. This automated guidance is designed to handle the application setup in a way that saves users thousands of dollars in legal fees, effectively making the process as simple as a standard online job application."

nodes.title: Cashfree Payments
nodes.description: Next-gen digital payments provider for Indian businesses. YC S17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.cashfree.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/cashfree-payments

Cashfree is a licensed payment aggregator in India that helps over 50,000 businesses collect and send money. Headquartered in Bengaluru with a team of 200, the company provides a suite of financial tools including an easy-to-integrate payment gateway with instant settlements, an API banking platform for bulk disbursals, and split payment solutions for marketplaces.

The platform also offers specialized infrastructure such as a dedicated UPI stack, a Bank Account Verification API, and Auto Collect, a virtual account solution that matches inbound payments to customers. Cashfree works with all leading banks to build the core payments and banking infrastructure that powers its products.

Notable customers include major Indian consumer and tech brands like Xiaomi, Nykaa, Zomato, Swiggy, and Shell, as well as donation platforms like Ketto and Milaap. The company is also integrated with major global and regional platforms such as Shopify, Wix, PayPal, Amazon Pay, Ola Money, and Google Pay.

_Usage:_

"How does Cashfree handle the complexity of Indian payment rails compared to standard global gateways?"

"Cashfree acts as a licensed payment aggregator that abstracts the complexity of working with multiple Indian banks by providing a unified API for gateways, payouts, and UPI. It handles the plumbing for instant settlements and refunds, and includes specific utilities like Bank Account Verification and Auto Collect to match virtual account payments to specific customers, which is critical for high-volume Indian e-commerce and marketplace operations."

nodes.title: Muzz
nodes.description: The world's largest Muslim dating app for marriage-focused matchmaking. YC S17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://muzz.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/muzz

Muzz is a mobile application designed specifically for single Muslims seeking marriage partners, operating on the premise that the community prioritizes marriage over casual dating. As the largest platform in this niche, it claims over 10 million members and has facilitated more than 500,000 weddings, addressing a significant gap in the global Muslim demographic.

Headquartered in London, the company was the first Muslim-centric startup to be backed by Y Combinator in Summer 2017. It has since raised $9 million in funding from Silicon Valley and global investors and maintains a team of 104 people. The platform has received coverage from major media outlets including the BBC, The New York Times, and TechCrunch.

By focusing on high-quality mobile experiences for a specific cultural and religious group, Muzz distinguishes itself in the crowded social networking space, aiming to transform how Muslims meet and marry across the globe.

_Usage:_

"How does Muzz differ from generalist dating apps like Tinder or Bumble in terms of user intent and target demographic?"

"Muzz is explicitly designed for Muslims who are looking to marry rather than date casually, which aligns with the cultural and religious norms of its target audience. While generalist apps often cater to a broader range of relationship goals, Muzz focuses on facilitating long-term commitments, resulting in a user base of over 10 million members who are specifically seeking a marriage partner within the Muslim community."

nodes.title: Pop Meals

Founded in the Summer 2017 Y Combinator batch, Pop Meals has raised over $28 million from Y Combinator and leading tech investors in Silicon Valley, Europe, and Asia. The company is currently expanding rapidly across the region.

nodes.title: FAZZ
nodes.description: All-in-one finance platform for Southeast Asian businesses. YC S17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://fazzfinancial.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fazz

FAZZ operates as a B2B neobank providing an all-in-one finance platform for businesses in Indonesia and Singapore. The company serves underbanked segments such as warungs and startups while building a super-app for mid-market and enterprise clients. Its core features include payment acceptance via e-wallets, bank transfers, and credit cards, alongside a business cash account that earns 4% interest.

The platform also offers transfer and pay capabilities through payment APIs, corporate cards, and invoice processing, as well as lending services with instant settlement and invoice financing. FAZZ integrates value-add SaaS tools for inventory and expense management to support comprehensive business operations.

With a team of 500 based in Jakarta, FAZZ processes over $6 billion in annualized gross transaction volume and has achieved $25 million in annualized revenue. The company has raised over $74 million from investors including Tiger Global, DST, Y Combinator, B Capital Group, and Insignia Ventures.

_Usage:_

"How does FAZZ differentiate itself from standard payment processors for small businesses in Southeast Asia?"

"FAZZ goes beyond simple payment acceptance by acting as a full B2B neobank that combines payments with a cash account earning 4% interest, lending products like invoice financing, and operational SaaS tools for inventory and expense management. This all-in-one approach is specifically designed for underbanked segments like warungs and startups in Indonesia and Singapore, allowing them to manage their entire financial stack within a single platform rather than relying on multiple disjointed services."

Dharma Labs, a San Francisco-based fintech company, built the only Ethereum wallet capable of seamlessly moving money between any US bank account and decentralized exchanges like Uniswap. The product was designed to look and feel like a mainstream exchange but with the power of DeFi, allowing users to invest in a vast universe of tokens and yield opportunities with a simple tap.

The company operated with a team of 14 people and focused on simplifying the complex process of interacting with decentralized finance. By connecting traditional banking infrastructure directly to the Ethereum network, Dharma removed significant friction for users wanting to access crypto assets without navigating multiple wallets or bridges.

Dharma Labs was acquired, marking the end of its independent operations as a YC-backed startup.

_Usage:_

"How did Dharma handle the transfer of funds from a traditional bank to a decentralized exchange like Uniswap?"

"Dharma acted as a bridge, allowing users to plug in their US bank account and move money directly to decentralized exchanges. This eliminated the need for users to manually manage gas fees or switch between multiple wallets, creating a seamless experience that felt like using a centralized exchange but with access to DeFi liquidity."

nodes.title: VIDA & Co.
nodes.description: Platform for unique products produced on-demand at mass-scale. YC S17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.shopvida.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/vida-and-co

VIDA & Co. operates as a marketplace and manufacturing platform that produces unique consumer goods only after they have been purchased. By creating an interconnected network of designers, producers, and consumers, the company aims to offer an alternative to homogeneous, disposable retail items. It focuses on bringing quality and ethical production standards back into the supply chain while ensuring that only wanted items are brought into the world.

The company was based in San Francisco and worked within the consumer, apparel, and cosmetics industries. It utilized innovations in design and technology to make high-quality products more accessible. VIDA & Co. has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does VIDA's on-demand model differ from traditional retail inventory management?"

"VIDA produces items only after they are purchased, which eliminates the risk of overstocking and reduces waste compared to traditional models where goods are manufactured in bulk before demand is confirmed. This approach connects global creators directly with consumers to ensure that production aligns strictly with actual demand."

nodes.title: LotusPay

nodes.title: Mystery.org
nodes.description: Mystery.org creates engaging video explanations for children’s science questions. YC S17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mystery.org | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mystery-org

Mystery.org began by compiling the 150 most common science questions children ask teachers, forming its Mystery Science collection. The platform reached more than 4 million children in 50 % of U.S. elementary schools, and it has sold thousands of schools without employing a single salesperson. Backed by Y Combinator, Learn Capital, and Reach Capital, the company has expanded its scope to answer all other questions children have, receiving over 500 k inquiries in the last 18 months and producing video explanations for each.

The company’s mission is to cultivate a generation of better thinkers by providing clear, visual explanations—essentially a visual Wikipedia for kids. Mystery.org was acquired in 2024, marking its success in the education sector.

_Usage:_

"How does Mystery.org manage to sell to thousands of schools without a traditional sales team?"

"Mystery.org relies on a self‑service model where schools can sign up online and access its content directly, enabling rapid scaling and eliminating the need for a conventional sales cycle."

nodes.title: Ajaib

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.ajaib.co.id/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/ajaib

Ajaib is an online brokerage that lets Indonesians trade stocks, ETFs and mutual funds. Founded in 2018, it has positioned itself as Indonesia's leading fintech platform, driven by a mission to educate the public on the importance of investing for the future.

Guided by principles of ownership, growth mindset and a will to win, Ajaib focuses on expanding financial inclusion by providing safe, trusted and affordable investment instruments. The company claims to have transformed how young Indonesians invest, and it now boasts over one million users on its platform.

With a team of 300 based in Jakarta and remote, Ajaib has become the third‑largest brokerage by transaction volume in Indonesia and is recognized as the fastest‑growing unicorn in Southeast Asia. The firm remains active and continues to grow its user base.

nodes.description: Developer-friendly API documentation and version control platform. YC S18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://useoptic.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/optic

Optic helps developers collaborate at scale and build better APIs. Its open source tools make it easy to document API changes, review each other's changes during code review, and catch breaking changes before they reach production.
Optic applies version control concepts to API behavior, taking ideas from Git, code review, and CI.
Optic was acquired in 2018 and is used by Snyk engineers daily to improve the Snyk API.

_Usage:_

"Does Optic replace Swagger or Postman for API documentation?"

"Optic does not replace Swagger or Postman; instead it adds version control and review capabilities on top of API documentation, allowing teams to track changes, review them during code review, and detect breaking changes before deployment."

"Stoic focuses on helping users identify the specific factors that influence their emotions and provides actionable steps to improve mood, rather than offering generic meditation or relaxation techniques. nodes.title: MyPetrolPump
nodes.description: On-demand fuel delivery service in India. YC S19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mypetrolpump.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mypetrolpump

India has 200 million vehicles but only 60 000 gas stations, creating long queues and congested roads while new stations are impractical due to high land prices. MyPetrolPump solves this by bringing fuel directly to doorsteps, targeting large‑volume fleet customers such as schools, cab rentals, freight logistics, tours, hospitals, hotels and real‑estate operators. The company has 5 000 registered customers, can serve 1 200 of them with its limited fleet, and has attracted 400 franchisee requests across the country.

Founded by a Shell veteran with nine years of global oil‑marketing experience, MyPetrolPump operates out of Bengaluru, Karnataka, and serves the B2B supply‑chain and logistics sector. With a team of 42, it has been acquired, marking its success in addressing a critical infrastructure gap in India.

_Usage:_

"How does MyPetrolPump manage fuel delivery logistics compared to traditional gas stations?"

"MyPetrolPump uses mobile refueling vehicles that travel directly to fleet customers, eliminating the need for vehicles to drive to fixed stations. This approach reduces dead mileage and improves productivity for large‑volume users, while the company’s founder’s experience in oil marketing ensures efficient supply‑chain management."

nodes.title: MarketForce
nodes.description: MarketForce is the SuperApp that lets African neighbourhood merchants source, order, and pay for inventory digitally while offering banking services. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://marketforce.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/marketforce

MarketForce is a fintech marketplace that empowers neighbourhood merchants in Africa to source, order, and pay for inventory digitally. It also provides a banking wallet with credit facilities, digital payment collection, and agency banking services, allowing merchants to resell digital financial services such as airtime, electricity tokens, and bill payments.

Since its incorporation in 2019, MarketForce has grown rapidly, operating in five Sub‑Saharan African markets and serving more than 200,000 merchants and 180 consumer brands. The company runs an asset‑light model and has built a team of 400 employees based in Nairobi, Kenya, positioning its platform as a SuperApp that blends e‑commerce, banking, and financial services into a single digital experience.

The company remains active and continues to expand its reach across Africa, positioning itself as a key player in the region’s digital commerce and financial inclusion ecosystem.

_Usage:_

"How does MarketForce's banking wallet differ from traditional merchant banking services?"

"MarketForce’s wallet offers instant credit lines and digital payment collection within the same app, letting merchants manage inventory orders and financial services in one place, unlike separate banking apps that require distinct accounts."

MarketForce is a fintech marketplace that empowers neighbourhood merchants in Africa to source, order, and pay for inventory digitally. It also provides a banking wallet with credit facilities, digital payment collection, and agency banking services, allowing merchants to resell digital financial services such as airtime, electricity tokens, and bill payments.

Since its incorporation in 2019, MarketForce has grown rapidly, operating in five Sub‑Saharan African markets and serving more than 200,000 merchants and 180 consumer brands. The company runs an asset‑light model and has built a team of 400 employees based in Nairobi, Kenya, positioning its platform as a SuperApp that blends e‑commerce, banking, and financial services into a single digital experience.

The company remains active and continues to expand its reach across Africa, positioning itself as a key player in the region’s digital commerce and financial inclusion ecosystem.
usage: How does MarketForce's banking wallet differ from traditional merchant banking services?

MarketForce’s wallet offers instant credit lines and digital payment collection within the same app, letting merchants manage inventory orders and financial services in one place, unlike separate banking apps that require distinct accounts.

nodes.title: Jeeves
nodes.description: International banking infrastructure for global startups. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.tryjeeves.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/jeeves

Jeeves is an all-in-one corporate spend and expense management platform designed for businesses operating in North America, Latin America, Europe, and the UK. The company operates on proprietary infrastructure that allows firms to establish their finance functions within minutes, supporting cash, corporate cards, and cross-border payments. It handles multiple currencies for payback and supports operations in regions including Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Mexico, the EU, the UK, and the US.

The platform combines several tools, including Jeeves Pay for international transfers to over 150 countries with same-day arrival capabilities, Jeeves Cards for physical and virtual global spending, and built-in expense management features. These tools are offered without monthly or software fees, and the service is trusted by more than 3,000 companies worldwide.

Jeeves has raised $380 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz, CRV, GIC, Tencent, Silicon Valley Bank, Stanford University, and Y Combinator to fuel its international expansion. The company currently employs 150 people and maintains offices in Miami and New York, alongside a remote workforce.

_Usage:_

"How does Jeeves handle cross-border payments compared to traditional banking?"

"Jeeves uses proprietary infrastructure to facilitate cross-border payments to over 150 countries, with transfers between North America, South America, and Europe arriving as quickly as the same day. It offers competitive FX rates and allows companies to spend and pay in their preferred currencies, eliminating the need for personal guarantees or long-term contracts."

nodes.title: Clover
nodes.description: An all-in-one visual notebook that transforms linear documents into an infinite surface for brainstorming and planning. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://cloverapp.co | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/clover

Clover is a productivity tool designed specifically for creatives, offering a new style of text editor built from the ground up to support creative thinking. Instead of forcing users into traditional linear documents, the platform allows them to explode content onto an infinite surface. This visual approach supports note-taking, brainstorming, mind-mapping, and task management in a more intuitive way.

The company, which operated with a small remote team based in New York, was acquired. This acquisition highlights the market interest in novel interfaces for knowledge work that move beyond standard word processing constraints.

_Usage:_

"How does Clover's infinite surface differ from standard linear documents or whiteboard tools?"

"Clover takes a hybrid approach by allowing you to take the text from a traditional document and expand it into a visual, infinite canvas. This lets you brainstorm and mind-map directly within the writing context rather than switching between a text editor and a separate whiteboard tool, making it easier to manage tasks and ideas visually without losing the structure of your writing."

nodes.title: Plerk
nodes.description: Plerk provides virtual cards for flexible employee benefits and perks across global teams. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.plerk.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/plerk

Plerk offers a fintech solution that allows companies to provide flexible benefits and perks to local and remote employees regardless of geography. The platform utilizes virtual cards to enable employees to choose their preferred merchants for various perks, while companies retain total control over budgets and receive a single consolidated bill.

The company, which was acquired by Minu.mx, operated with a team of 28 people based in Guadalajara, Jal., Mexico, and remotely. It focused on B2B operations, helping organizations deploy funds for general or granular perk programs while giving employees the autonomy to decide what they truly need.

_Usage:_

"How does Plerk handle the complexity of paying for employee perks across different countries?"

"Plerk solves this by issuing virtual cards that allow employees to spend directly at local merchants, bypassing the need for centralized procurement in every region. Companies set the budget and program rules, but employees choose the specific vendors, and the company receives one bill for all transactions, simplifying accounting for distributed teams."

nodes.title: Charityvest
nodes.description: A modern donor-advised fund platform for individuals and corporations to make tax-smart charitable contributions. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.charityvest.org | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/charityvest

Charityvest operates as a modern donor-advised fund (DAF) designed for both individual and corporate donors. The platform allows users to contribute various asset classes, including cash, stock, crypto, and equity, to their charitable accounts. These balances can then be invested in low-cost ETFs to achieve tax-free growth.

The service streamlines the granting process by enabling users to send funds to over 1.4 million charities through a simple interface. It also consolidates tax reporting by providing a single tax receipt for all charitable giving activities. Based in Atlanta, Georgia, the company was part of the YC Summer 2020 batch with a team of nine people.

Charityvest has since been acquired, marking the conclusion of its independent operation as a YC-backed startup.

_Usage:_

"How does Charityvest handle the tax implications of different asset types compared to traditional giving methods?"

"It allows you to contribute cash, stock, crypto, and equity directly to your donor-advised fund, which lets you take a tax deduction on the contribution while the assets grow tax-free in low-cost ETFs. Instead of managing separate receipts for each donation, you get one consolidated tax receipt for all your giving, simplifying the accounting for both individuals and corporations."

nodes.title: Chipax
nodes.description: Chipax provides real-time accounts receivable and payable management for small and medium businesses in Latin America. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.chipax.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/chipax

Chipax operates as a financial operations platform for small and medium businesses, primarily in Mexico and Chile. The company handles payments, invoicing, and reconciliations to deliver real-time visibility into accounts receivable and accounts payable. It serves over 1,100 paying businesses and has reached $1.6M in annual recurring revenue.

Founded by engineers with firsthand experience in SMB financial management, Chipax addresses the complexity of traditional accounting tools. The team is based in Santiago, Chile, and operates remotely, with a current size of 37 employees. As an active YC Summer 2021 company, it focuses on simplifying financial workflows for the Latin American market.

_Usage:_

"How does Chipax differ from traditional accounting software like QuickBooks for SMBs in Latam?"

"While traditional tools often require manual reconciliation and batch processing, Chipax automates the entire cycle of payments, invoices, and reconciliations. This provides real-time AR and AP data rather than static reports, which is particularly useful for businesses in Mexico and Chile that need immediate visibility into their cash flow without manual data entry."

nodes.title: Luable
nodes.description: A Latin American marketplace connecting retail depositors with banks for faster and cheaper funding. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mejorcdt.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/luable

Luable operates a bank deposits marketplace in Latin America that allows financial institutions to source funding from retail users. This model offers banks a faster and more cost-effective alternative to traditional expansion methods like opening physical branch offices or hiring additional sales representatives.

The platform aggregates multiple banks in a single interface, enabling retail users to compare options and select products that best fit their needs. It also supports emerging banks by allowing them to offer a full digital experience without incurring fixed costs associated with physical infrastructure.

Founded in 2021 and based in Bogotá, Colombia, Luable has processed over USD $30 million in deposits for various banks. The company, which has a team of 40, is currently expanding its operations from Colombia into Mexico and the Caribbean.

_Usage:_

"How does Luable's funding model differ from traditional bank expansion strategies?"

"Instead of banks spending capital on physical branches or large sales teams to acquire depositors, Luable acts as a digital intermediary. It aggregates retail users who are looking for deposit products, allowing banks to access this liquidity pool directly. This reduces the customer acquisition cost for the bank while providing users with a comparison tool to find the best rates across different institutions."

Instead of banks spending capital on physical branches or large sales teams to acquire depositors, Luable acts as a digital intermediary. It aggregates retail users who are looking for deposit products, allowing banks to access this liquidity pool directly. This reduces the customer acquisition cost for the bank while providing users with a comparison tool to find the best rates across different institutions.

Payhippo is a fintech company that provides loans to small and medium-sized enterprises in Africa, specifically targeting the Nigerian market. The company operates with a team of 11 people based in Lagos, Nigeria, and Los Angeles, California.

The platform is designed for speed, delivering credit to small businesses in under three hours. In July 2021, Payhippo reported generating $42k in revenue in Nigeria, accompanied by a 25% month-over-month growth rate and a 97% repayment rate.

"Payhippo cuts the typical wait time for SME loans down to under three hours, which is significantly faster than conventional banking processes. This speed is supported by a high repayment rate of 97%, suggesting that the rapid disbursement model does not come at the cost of credit risk."

nodes.title: Aleph Solutions (Alephee)
nodes.description: enables automotive aftermarket brands to manage and sell parts online via marketplaces. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.alephee.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/aleph-solutions-alephee

Aleph Solutions helps automotive aftermarket brands, including companies with thousands of products, increase their revenue in Latin America by listing their inventory on major e-commerce sites like Mercado Libre and Amazon. The platform addresses the challenge of maintaining up-to-date catalogs, prices, and inventory across digital channels, a task that is difficult for brands and resellers to manage without dedicated tools.

By creating high-quality product catalogs, Aleph allows brands to replicate their offline reseller networks online. This infrastructure enables any authorized seller to access the brand's product data and list items on marketplaces, streamlining the shift to digital sales. The company reports that its customers sell over U$D 4 million worth of product every month using its software.

Based in Buenos Aires, Argentina, and operating remotely, Aleph Solutions is an active B2B e-commerce company with a team of approximately 60 people. It serves the retail and marketplace sectors by providing the necessary tools for brands and wholesalers to manage complex product data at scale.

_Usage:_

"How does Aleph handle the complexity of managing thousands of SKUs across different marketplaces like Amazon and Mercado Libre?"

"Aleph acts as a central hub where brands create and maintain high-quality product catalogs. Instead of each reseller manually updating prices and inventory for thousands of items, they access the brand's centralized catalog through Aleph's software. This ensures that when a reseller lists a part on a marketplace, the data is accurate and synchronized, allowing brands to scale their online presence without the overhead of managing each individual listing."

nodes.title: Whalesync
nodes.description: Two-way real-time data syncing between website builders and collaboration tools like Airtable and Notion. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.whalesync.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/whalesync

Whalesync is an automation platform that simplifies data management by syncing content between website builders such as Webflow, Wix, and WordPress, and collaboration tools like Airtable, Notion, and Google Sheets. By enabling two-way, real-time synchronization, the company allows marketing teams to manage their websites directly from the tools they already use for daily operations.

Launched during Y Combinator’s Summer 2021 cohort, Whalesync has grown to a team of eight based in St. Petersburg, Florida, and remote locations. The platform is trusted by hundreds of companies, including Ramp, Webflow, and Alchemy, and processes millions of transactions daily to keep website content aligned with business data.

_Usage:_

"How does Whalesync differ from standard webhooks or manual content updates?"

"Whalesync provides two-way, real-time synchronization, meaning changes made in Airtable or Notion automatically update the website, and vice versa. This eliminates the need for manual copy-pasting or building custom webhook integrations for each specific tool combination, allowing marketing teams to manage site content directly within their existing collaboration workflows."

nodes.title: Locale
nodes.description: Delivering organic, high-protein meals designed for longevity. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.shoplocale.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/locale

Locale creates organic high-protein meals that prioritize longevity through strict nutritional standards. Each meal contains 40-60g of protein, utilizes nutrient-dense meat sources such as grass-fed and pasture-raised options, and includes over 8g of fiber. The company avoids seed oils, processed ingredients, and refined sugars, instead cooking with extra virgin olive oil and using organic, pesticide-free produce.

The brand emphasizes clean eating by ensuring its products are microplastic-free and high in anti-inflammatories and Omega-3s. Meals are packaged in reusable glass jars to support sustainability. Since launching in 2020, Locale has delivered over 100,000 orders and is backed by investors including a16z, Y Combinator, and Goodwater.

_Usage:_

"What specific nutritional metrics does Locale guarantee per meal compared to standard meal kits?"

"Locale guarantees 40-60g of protein and at least 8g of fiber per meal, while explicitly excluding seed oils, refined sugars, and processed ingredients. It also ensures the produce is organic and pesticide-free, and the packaging is microplastic-free reusable glass, distinguishing it from conventional delivery services that often use plastic and lower-protein profiles."

"It functions as a virtual co-working space where you join high-intensity sprints with other members. nodes.title: Stipop
nodes.description: Monetization platform enabling character creators to generate revenue directly from their audience. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://studio.stipop.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/stipop

Stipop operates as a monetization platform for independent character IP owners, often described as a Patreon for character creators. The company provides fun, dynamic features that allow creators to generate revenue directly from their audience. It is a team of eight based in Los Angeles and Santa Monica, California.

The platform evolved from a sticker service that hosted 5,000 creators and 250,000 stickers. During this earlier phase, Stipop supplied stickers to major platforms including Canva, Microsoft Teams, Google, and Adobe. It also offers a sticker API and SDK designed to help chat apps improve user engagement and revenue.

Stipop is an active company from the Summer 2021 YC batch. It has received investment from Snap through the Yellow Accelerator, Y Combinator, Translink Investment, Strong Ventures, and Next Ventures.

_Usage:_

"How does Stipop differ from general creator platforms like Patreon, and what infrastructure do they offer to third-party apps?"

"Stipop is specifically tailored for character IP owners rather than general content creators, focusing on dynamic features for character-based revenue. Beyond the creator platform, it provides a sticker API and SDK that chat apps can integrate to boost their own user engagement and monetization, having previously supplied stickers to major platforms like Canva and Adobe."

nodes.title: Nasdisc
nodes.description: A marketplace for buying and selling vinyl, cassettes, and CDs. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.nasdisc.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/nasdisc

Nasdisc is a San Francisco-based marketplace designed to facilitate the buying and selling of physical music media, including vinyl, cassettes, and CDs. The company addresses a fragmented secondary market where existing platforms often lack robust transaction processing capabilities, despite facilitating hundreds of millions of dollars in annual exchanges. By taking a 12% commission on sales, Nasdisc positions itself to capture value from a rapidly expanding industry where record prices have been skyrocketing due to supply constraints and high demand.

The startup was founded by a team of four software engineers who previously worked at Google and other tech roles, leveraging their technical background to build a more user-friendly trading platform. They launched their website in late 2021, quickly amassing $50,000 in listings and generating initial weekly sales of $1,000. The company has since been acquired, marking a successful exit for this niche e-commerce venture.

_Usage:_

"How does Nasdisc handle the transaction process compared to other vinyl marketplaces?"

"Unlike other dedicated marketplaces that may not process transactions directly, Nasdisc handles the full transaction flow, taking a 12% cut of each sale. This integrated approach aims to solve the usability and payment friction found in existing platforms, making it easier for buyers and sellers to complete deals on physical media."

nodes.title: Onfolk
nodes.description: Gusto for the UK, simplifying payroll and HR for growing teams. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://onfolk.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/onfolk

Onfolk provides a unified platform for payroll and human resources management, designed to replace fragmented spreadsheets and poorly integrated tools. The company enables growing teams to run payroll in one minute, onboard new starters in two minutes, and manage centralized employee information, time-off, and reporting. It also offers hands-off integrations for pensions and accounting.

Founded by software engineers who previously spent four years scaling Monzo, Onfolk was built to address the inefficiencies of traditional payroll providers. The team leveraged their experience to create a product they felt was missing from the market, aiming to streamline the administrative burden on modern companies.

Onfolk has since been acquired, marking a significant milestone for the London-based startup. It holds certification as a payroll software from the UK government, underscoring its compliance and reliability in the B2B human resources sector.

_Usage:_

nodes.title: MadEats
nodes.description: Online delivery-only restaurant group in the Philippines building affordable food brands via ghost kitchens. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/madeats

MadEats is a delivery-only restaurant group based in Makati, Philippines, that operates through its own network of ghost kitchens. By eliminating the costs associated with physical dining areas and wait staff, the company redirects resources toward improving food quality, growing its food brands, and enhancing the delivery experience. This model allows MadEats to maintain high margins while offering affordable options to consumers.

The company was selected for the Y Combinator Summer 2021 batch and has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does using ghost kitchens change the unit economics compared to a traditional brick-and-mortar restaurant?"

"It removes the capital and operational costs of maintaining a physical dining space and hiring front-of-house staff. This allows the company to allocate more budget directly to food production, brand development, and delivery logistics, resulting in higher margins for the same end product."

nodes.title: Beeper
nodes.description: A unified chat app that aggregates 15+ messaging networks into a single interface with advanced search and filtering. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://beeper.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/beeper

Beeper is a consumer application designed to solve the fragmentation of modern messaging by connecting to over 15 different chat networks within a single interface. It offers features such as unified search and advanced filtering, allowing users to manage communications across platforms like iMessage and Android-based services without switching apps. The company operates with a team of 16 people, with locations in San Francisco, Palo Alto, and remote positions.

The platform is available on Desktop, Android, iPhone, and iPad, aiming to eliminate the friction of remembering which specific app was used for a particular conversation or locating shared media. By consolidating these disparate channels, Beeper seeks to boost communication efficiency for users who interact across multiple ecosystems.

Beeper was acquired, marking a significant milestone in the consumer messaging space.

_Usage:_

"How does Beeper handle the lack of native cross-platform support between systems like iMessage and Android?"

"Beeper acts as a bridge by connecting to these separate networks simultaneously, providing a unified inbox where you can send and receive messages across different platforms without needing to install or switch between individual apps."

nodes.title: SolarMente
nodes.description: Home electrification at $0 upfront cost. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://solarmente.es | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/solarmente

SolarMente enabled homeowners in Southern Europe to install solar panels, energy storage, and heat pumps with zero upfront cost. The company operated on a model where users paid through predictable monthly savings rather than a large initial capital expenditure. Based in Barcelona with a team of 65, SolarMente raised $5M from investors including Y Combinator, Climate Capital, and Leonardo DiCaprio. The company has since become inactive.

_Usage:_

"How did SolarMente handle the capital intensity of home electrification for consumers?"

"They removed the upfront barrier entirely by covering the installation costs for solar, storage, and heat pumps. Homeowners then repaid the investment through the predictable monthly savings generated by the new energy system, effectively turning a capital expenditure into a subscription-like cash flow model."

nodes.title: Hedgehog
nodes.description: A cryptocurrency robo-adviser that manages funds in broad baskets of digital assets. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://hedgehog.app | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/hedgehog

Hedgehog is a crypto robo-adviser designed to manage user funds by investing in broad baskets of digital assets that cover up to 85% of the cryptocurrency market cap. The company, which has since become inactive, operated out of San Francisco and San Jose with a small remote team. At its peak, the platform served 15,000 users monitoring $176 million in crypto assets, with over $548,000 in gross transaction volume on its initial product version. The company completed its exit interview with the SEC in April 2024 and made its custodial product available on the App Store and Google Play.

_Usage:_

"Hedgehog completed its exit interview with the SEC in April 2024, which is a standard part of the regulatory process for fintech and crypto companies. They also launched a custodial product on major app stores, indicating they moved toward regulated self-custody solutions for their users."

nodes.title: FoodCourt
nodes.description: Operating virtual restaurants and dark stores to make food and convenience goods more accessible across Africa. YC S22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.getfoodcourt.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/foodcourt

FoodCourt, also known as CoKitchen, operates as Africa's leading virtual restaurant company, utilizing a network of ghost kitchens and dark stores to serve over 350,000 meals in the last 12 months. The company is headquartered in Lagos, Nigeria, with a team of 80 employees.

To address the unique challenges of the African on-demand food delivery market, FoodCourt adopts a full-stack approach that controls key areas of the value chain, including technology, production, and delivery. This strategy allows the company to provide users with a seamless and consistent experience while maintaining the flexibility needed for rapid growth.

By focusing on making good food and quick convenience goods more accessible, FoodCourt aims to expand its reach across the continent through its integrated virtual infrastructure.

_Usage:_

"How does FoodCourt's full-stack approach differ from standard food delivery apps that just connect users to existing restaurants?"

"Unlike standard delivery platforms that act as middlemen for existing brick-and-mortar restaurants, FoodCourt controls the entire value chain by operating its own virtual restaurants and dark stores. This means it manages the technology, production, and delivery layers directly, which allows it to offer a more consistent user experience and greater flexibility for scaling without relying on third-party restaurant partners."

nodes.title: Supr Daily
nodes.description: Supr Daily delivers daily groceries to Indian households by 7 am using a milk‑subscription model. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.suprdaily.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/supr-daily

Supr Daily is a daily grocery delivery service operating in India. It uses a daily milk subscription as a “railroad” to bundle deliveries, cutting last‑mile costs by tenfold and enabling a “Trojan Cow” approach that brings all groceries to the doorstep by 7 am each morning.

At its peak the company generated a $100 million annual revenue run rate, operated in six cities and fulfilled more than 200 k orders per day. Supr Daily was part of Y Combinator’s Winter 2017 batch and was later acquired by Swiggy.

_Usage:_

"How does Supr Daily’s milk‑subscription model lower delivery costs compared to standard grocery delivery services?"

"Supr Daily bundles grocery trips with a daily milk subscription, treating the milk delivery route as a fixed “railroad”. By piggybacking other items onto that route, it spreads the last‑mile expense across many orders, which the company says reduces those costs by about ten times."

nodes.title: Arthena
nodes.description: Arthena offers data‑driven funds that give investors exposure to the liquid, low‑volatility segment of the art market. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.arthena.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/arthena

Arthena provides a financial product that lets high‑net‑worth individuals invest in the alternative asset class of art through a traditional fund structure. By focusing on the most liquid segment of the market, the company aims to deliver growth that is uncorrelated with traditional investments and characterized by low volatility.

The firm has built a statistically rigorous model that estimates artwork values over time using auction records and repeat‑sale data. Features such as artist name, medium, creation date, origin, and size are used to group similar works, calculate expected ROI and volatility, and run Monte Carlo simulations that produce annualized returns and Sharpe ratios. This data‑driven approach validates the financial viability of its funds.

Arthena was acquired after its Winter 2017 batch, reflecting the market’s interest in quantifying art as an investment. The company operates out of New York City with a team of twelve.

_Usage:_

"How does Arthena’s valuation model differ from a typical art appraisal service?"

"Arthena’s model relies on quantitative data from auction records and repeat sales, using features like artist, medium, date, origin, and size to group similar works and then applying Monte Carlo analysis to estimate ROI, volatility, and Sharpe ratios, whereas traditional appraisals are usually qualitative and based on expert opinion rather than statistical simulation."

nodes.body:

Sqreen is an application security platform used by more than 800 organizations to protect, observe, and test their applications, APIs, and microservices. Sqreen was acquired after establishing a presence in the B2B security market; the company, founded in YC’s Winter 2018 batch and based in San Francisco, employs around 120 people.

"Sqreen monitors the actual execution of code inside the application, analyzing behavior in real time rather than relying on predefined attack signatures. nodes.title: Universe
nodes.description: Universe enables users to design and launch websites from their iPhone, iPad, or Mac. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://onuniverse.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/universe

Universe is a website builder that works primarily on mobile devices. Its app lets anyone create a great‑looking site and start selling online in minutes from an iPhone, iPad, or Mac, and the experience is described as fun as playing with Legos. The company positions itself as the first website builder designed for phones, and it showcases examples of sites built on its platform.

Universe is a remote‑first company of about 25 employees spread across the United States. It graduated from Y Combinator’s Winter 2018 batch and has raised $17.2 million from investors including Google Ventures, General Catalyst, Javelin Venture Partners, and Box Group. The team emphasizes individual agency, freedom to work from anywhere, and a culture of rapid learning.

_Usage:_

"Can I create a full e‑commerce website using only the Universe iPhone app?"

"Yes. Universe’s mobile app lets you design a site, add products, and start selling online directly from an iPhone or iPad, so you can launch an e‑commerce store without needing a desktop computer."

nodes.title: Modern Health
nodes.description: Modern Health provides a mental health benefits platform for employers. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.modernhealth.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/modern-health

Modern Health is the leading mental wellness platform that combines clinically validated assessments, personalized stress management support, an international network of certified behavioral health coaches, and licensed therapists to deliver mental health support across a broad range of individual needs. It empowers employers to help employees be less stressed, more engaged, and happier through evidence‑based technology and professional support.

The company has raised over $170M from investors including Battery Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, and John Doerr, and it supports more than 200 companies worldwide such as Lyft, Pixar, and Okta. With a team of 375 people operating from Boston, San Francisco, and remotely, Modern Health serves a global client base in the healthcare services sector.

_Usage:_

"How is Modern Health different from a typical employee assistance program?"

"Modern Health goes beyond standard EAPs by offering clinically validated assessments and a personalized stress‑management plan, plus access to a vetted network of certified coaches and licensed therapists, all delivered through its evidence‑based platform."

nodes.title: Shogun
nodes.description: Shogun enables brands to build high‑converting ecommerce experiences. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://getshogun.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/shogun

Shogun is an ecommerce experience platform that helps brands drive higher conversions, revenue, and brand loyalty. Its two main products, Shogun Page Builder and Shogun Frontend, let teams build and optimize online stores. The platform integrates with major ecommerce services such as Shopify and BigCommerce, allowing customers to use familiar back‑ends while enhancing the front‑end experience.

The company serves more than 20,000 customers, including brands like Leesa, MVMT, Timbuk2, and Chubbies. Shogun operates as a remote‑first, inclusive organization with about 90 employees spread across San Francisco, Palo Alto, and other remote locations. It is part of the Winter 2018 Y Combinator batch and remains active in the B2B SaaS e‑commerce space.

_Usage:_

"Does Shogun replace the native page‑builder features in Shopify?"

"Shogun provides its own Page Builder and Frontend that integrate with Shopify, so teams can use Shogun’s tools to design and optimize their stores while still running on Shopify’s platform."

nodes.title: Look After My Bills
nodes.description: Look After My Bills automatically switches users to the cheapest energy deals. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.lookaftermybills.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/look-after-my-bills

Look After My Bills is an auto‑switching service that continuously checks energy tariffs and moves customers onto the best available deal without manual effort. By handling the comparison and switch process each year, it aims to keep households paying the lowest possible price for electricity and gas.

The company was acquired after its Winter 2018 Y Combinator batch, reflecting the value of its automated bill‑optimisation technology. Based in England, it operated with a two‑person team focused on the fintech and consumer‑finance markets.

_Usage:_

"How does Look After My Bills find a cheaper energy plan compared to doing it yourself?"

"It runs an automated service that monitors the market for energy tariffs and triggers a switch whenever a lower‑priced option becomes available, eliminating the need for users to manually compare rates each year."

nodes.title: Qulture.Rocks
nodes.description: Qulture.Rocks offers an operating system that unifies people, performance, and culture management for startups. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://qulture.rocks/en/home/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/qulture-rocks

Qulture.Rocks builds people management, OKR management, and culture management software for some of the world’s most innovative companies. The company is backed by investors such as Founders Fund, Blackstone, Sequoia, and Tiger Global.
Its product suite covers 1:1 meetings, engagement surveys, performance reviews, OKRs/goals, ongoing feedback, and peer‑to‑peer recognition, and it integrates seamlessly with existing software including Slack. Qulture.Rocks also assists customers in designing their people processes, which is especially helpful for startups and scale‑ups implementing these practices for the first time.
Qulture.Rocks was acquired, and it now operates with a team of about 70 people out of San Francisco.

_Usage:_

"Can Qulture.Rocks integrate with our current Slack workspace, or do we need a separate HR system?"

"Qulture.Rocks integrates directly with existing tools such as Slack, allowing teams to run 1:1s, surveys, OKRs, and recognition within the same environment without requiring a separate platform."

nodes.title: Swipehouse

nodes.body:

Swipehouse is the biggest social network in the world for TikTok celebrities, offering creators daily matches with brands. It was one of the first five U.S. companies to receive access to the TikTok API, which helped fuel its rapid growth. In its first year the platform launched over 400 companies on TikTok and works with partners such as Ridge and Hopper. Swipehouse was acquired in 2021. The five‑person team operates out of Boston and Cambridge, focusing on entertainment, community, and e‑commerce for creators.

"Swipehouse leverages its early TikTok API access to automatically generate daily match suggestions for creators, directly linking them with brands like Ridge and Hopper, whereas many other platforms rely on manual outreach or less frequent matchmaking cycles."
