nodes.title: YouTeam
nodes.description: YouTeam matches startups with top offshore engineers through an exclusive talent marketplace. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://youteam.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/youteam

YouTeam provides a platform that connects startups with select offshore developers seeking full‑time contracts, sourcing talent that isn’t listed on freelance portals or job boards. It is the only service accessing this previously untapped pool, allowing it to surface the “crème de la crème” of engineers.

The marketplace has helped more than 60 YC startups hire top‑notch engineers they couldn’t find elsewhere, establishing it as a trusted recruiting partner in the B2B talent space.

YouTeam was acquired, reflecting its value to the market. The company operates from San Francisco and Mountain View with a team of 34 employees.

"YouTeam taps into a curated offshore talent pool that isn’t posted on public freelance portals or job boards, then selects the highest‑quality candidates for full‑time contracts, giving startups access to engineers they otherwise couldn’t reach."

nodes.title: Dataform
nodes.description: Dataform lets data teams build, version control, and deploy SQL pipelines in Snowflake, BigQuery, and Redshift. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://dataform.co | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dataform

Dataform provides a platform for data teams to build, version‑control, and deploy SQL pipelines directly in their cloud data warehouses such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and Redshift. It streamlines the workflow by treating SQL code as software, enabling collaborative development and reliable deployments.

The company was acquired by Google Cloud in December 2020, giving Google Cloud a native solution for managing analytics pipelines. At the time of acquisition Dataform had a ten‑person team based in London and was positioned in the B2B analytics space.

_Usage:_

"How does Dataform differ from managing raw SQL scripts with a separate Git repo?"

"Dataform bundles version‑control, dependency tracking, and warehouse‑native execution into a single platform, so teams can develop and deploy pipelines without building a custom CI/CD pipeline for raw SQL scripts."

nodes.title: CodeStream
nodes.description: CodeStream provides a developer collaboration platform that lets engineers request code review feedback directly from their IDE. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://codestream.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/codestream

CodeStream offers IDE plugins that simplify code reviews by allowing developers to request feedback on a snapshot of their repository with a single command. The platform can capture uncommitted and unpushed code, enabling engineers to verify work‑in‑progress before committing. It also supports the traditional workflow of committing and pushing at the end of a sprint.

CodeStream was acquired, highlighting its relevance in the B2B engineering and product design space. The company operates with a team of about ten people across New York and remote locations, delivering a SaaS collaboration tool for developers.

_Usage:_

"How does CodeStream let me get review feedback on code that isn’t yet committed compared to using a standard pull‑request process?"

"CodeStream’s IDE plugin adds a command that captures the current state of your repo—including uncommitted and unpushed changes—and sends that snapshot for review, so you can get feedback without creating a commit or push. Traditional pull‑request workflows require you to commit and push changes before reviewers can see them."

Traditional pull‑request workflows require you to commit and push changes before reviewers can see them.

nodes.title: Eclipse Foods
nodes.description: Eclipse Foods creates plant‑based dairy products that replicate the taste, texture, and functionality of conventional milk. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.eclipsefoods.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/eclipse-foods

Eclipse Foods has built the world’s first plant‑based dairy platform that uses micelles – the microscopic structures found in milk – to produce products that taste, feel, and perform like traditional dairy. The company says its approach lets it transform the roughly $500 billion dairy industry with sustainable, healthy, and humane alternatives.

The San Francisco‑based startup has raised over $60 million from investors including Y Combinator, the chairman of Beyond Meat, the founder of Reddit, the creator of Gmail, Forerunner Ventures, Sozo Ventures, and Initialized Capital. Its mission is to create a more sustainable food system by offering plant‑based foods that require no sacrifice.

_Usage:_

"How does Eclipse Foods get plant‑based milk to taste and behave like real dairy without using any animal ingredients?"

"Eclipse Foods leverages micelles, the tiny structures that give milk its characteristic properties, in a proprietary plant‑based platform. By replicating these micelles with plant ingredients, the company can produce products that match the taste, texture, and functionality of conventional dairy."

nodes.title: Pronto
nodes.description: Pronto provides a ride‑sharing and delivery platform for second‑tier cities in Latin America. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.tuprontomx.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pronto

Pronto is the first ride‑sharing and delivery platform built specifically for second‑tier cities in Latin America, where cash transactions dominate. Because cash payments make the Uber commission model impractical, Pronto charges drivers a monthly subscription ranging from $59 to $99 based on their revenue, which yields higher lifetime value, low customer acquisition cost, and strong driver engagement. Since launch the company has processed over 2,000,000 trips, serving more than 200,000 users, and after bootstrapping to half a million trips it joined Y Combinator’s Winter 2019 batch. It targets a market of over 14,000 second‑tier cities and 500 million people lacking access to ride‑sharing platforms. The team of 62 operates from Mexico City.

_Usage:_

"How does Pronto make money if most rides are paid in cash?"

"Pronto bypasses cash commissions by charging drivers a recurring subscription fee of $59‑$99 per month, which is tied to the driver’s monthly revenue. This subscription model creates a predictable revenue stream for the company while keeping the service free for riders who pay cash."

nodes.title: Our World in Data

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://ourworldindata.org/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/our-world-in-data

Our World in Data publishes an open-access platform that lets users explore the state of the world through interactive data visualizations and summaries of scientific literature. It covers topics ranging from global poverty and health to climate change and education, offering 3405 charts across 297 topics.

The service is free, open-source, and positioned as a public good, attracting millions of monthly users and frequent citations in research and media worldwide. With a team of 19 located in Oxford and remote, it operates in the education sector as a nonprofit organization.

The organization remains active, continuously adding new visualizations to help people understand progress and setbacks on the world’s largest problems.

"Our World in Data not only provides raw data but also pairs it with interactive visualizations and concise summaries of the scientific literature, all under a free, open-source license. This focus on storytelling and education, plus its breadth of 3405 charts across 297 topics, makes it a distinct public‑good resource compared with more data‑only platforms."

nodes.title: Dagger
nodes.description: Dagger provides a programmable CI/CD engine that runs pipelines as code in containers. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://dagger.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/dagger

Dagger is a programmable CI/CD engine that executes pipelines as standard OCI containers. Developers can write pipelines in the same programming language as their application using a chosen SDK, allowing pipelines to be treated as code. The engine offers instant local testing, superior default caching, and full portability, so the same pipeline can run on a developer’s machine, a CI runner, a dedicated server, or any container hosting service.

Because Dagger runs entirely within the Docker ecosystem, it integrates with existing container workflows and lets teams use each other’s tools without learning new languages. Its cross‑language instrumentation and caching work consistently across environments, making it a flexible DevSecOps solution for B2B engineering teams.

The company, founded in the Winter 2019 batch, has a distributed team of 22 across multiple global locations and remains active in the developer tools space.

_Usage:_

"Can I run the same Dagger pipeline locally and on a CI runner without modifying it?"

"Yes. Dagger packages pipelines as standard OCI containers, so the exact same pipeline can be executed on a local machine, a CI runner, or any container hosting service without changes, providing instant local testing and consistent caching across environments."

nodes.title: Kalshi
nodes.description: Kalshi operates the first federally regulated exchange for trading event outcomes. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.kalshi.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/kalshi

Kalshi is the first federally regulated exchange where people can trade on the outcome of events. It is regulated by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) as the first legal futures exchange in the United States for a broad category of events.

The company has created a new asset class called “event contracts,” allowing traders to capitalize on everyday knowledge by expanding what can be traded. Kalshi’s platform enables users to buy and sell contracts tied to real‑world events, effectively turning opinions into tradable assets.

Based in New York City with a team of about 125 employees, Kalshi continues to develop its exchange and grow the event‑contract market.

_Usage:_

"How is trading on Kalshi different from trading traditional futures?"

"Kalshi trades event contracts that settle based on the outcome of real‑world events rather than price movements of commodities or financial instruments. Because the contracts are tied to discrete events, the market lets participants bet on things like election results or weather outcomes, and the exchange is regulated by the CFTC as a legal futures market."

ZeroDown offers an alternative to the rent-or-own dilemma by purchasing a home outright on behalf of a professional renter and allowing them to pay rent that builds purchase credits. A portion of each payment accrues toward ownership, and tenants can decide when to use those credits to buy the home from ZeroDown. "ZeroDown actually buys the home with cash and then rents it to the tenant, with part of each rent payment credited toward eventual purchase, whereas traditional rent‑to‑own typically involves the tenant leasing from the seller and may not provide a clear path to equity buildup."

nodes.title: Accept.inc (formerly BoardRE)
nodes.description: Accept.inc lets homebuyers secure all‑cash offers and close in days by buying the property upfront and financing later. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.accept.inc | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/accept-inc

Accept.inc (formerly BoardRE) operates as an intermediary buyer that uses its own cash to purchase homes for the majority of buyers who need a mortgage, removing the lender from the transaction. This lets sellers and agents close in as little as two to three days while buyers lock in price before their mortgage closes.

The “Buy Now. Mortgage Later” model gives any qualified buyer an all‑cash deal, distinguishing Accept.inc from iBuyer firms that flip properties. It works with national lenders to assess creditworthiness up front and uses a short‑term credit facility to fund purchases.

Accept.inc was acquired after building a team of about 80 people in Denver and positioning itself at the intersection of fintech and real estate.

_Usage:_

"How does Accept.inc’s “Buy Now. Mortgage Later” model differ from traditional iBuyer services?"

"Accept.inc doesn’t buy, fix, and resell homes itself; instead it uses its cash to purchase a buyer’s chosen property and then offers a short‑term credit facility while the buyer secures a mortgage, allowing the transaction to close in 2‑3 days with an all‑cash offer, unlike iBuyers that profit by flipping properties."

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.theforage.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/forage

Forage partners with leading companies to create free digital learning simulations that mimic a day in the life of a junior employee. Students complete hypothetical tasks, learn from employees, and see which roles match their interests and skills. The platform currently serves over 4 million students.
Employers such as GE, BCG, HSBC, Goldman Sachs, Lululemon, EY, Accenture, JPMorgan Chase & Co, and many others use the simulations to attract high‑intent candidates from diverse backgrounds and to identify talent for hiring. The company’s model is built on the belief that talent is evenly distributed while opportunity is not.
Forage was acquired and now operates with a team of 65 people across San Francisco and remote locations.

_Usage:_

"Forage’s simulations are free, online experiences built with partner companies that let students complete mock tasks and receive feedback, providing a “day in the life” view without requiring on‑site placement or compensation. Unlike traditional internships, they are open to any student regardless of university or location, and they serve as a recruiting tool for companies to evaluate and attract talent."

nodes.description: Supabase is the easiest way to get started with Postgres. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://supabase.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/supabase

Supabase provides a fully managed Postgres environment that lets developers spin up isolated clusters in minutes, giving them instant database setup and a simple web interface. Each project comes with built‑in authentication, row‑level security, realtime data streams, and auto‑generating APIs, enabling teams to scale their applications independently while keeping all the features needed for production.

The company is 100% remote, with a team of 120 employees headquartered in San Francisco, CA, and operating worldwide. Founded in the Summer 2020 batch, Supabase targets B2B infrastructure customers and is positioned as an open‑source, developer‑tools alternative to proprietary database services.

_Usage:_

"How does Supabase’s auto‑generating API feature simplify backend development compared to manually building REST endpoints?"

"Supabase automatically exposes every table and view in a project as a RESTful endpoint, eliminating the need for developers to write boilerplate code for CRUD operations. This feature integrates directly with the Postgres cluster, so changes to the schema are reflected instantly in the API, streamlining rapid iteration and reducing maintenance overhead."

nodes.title: Tranch
nodes.description: Provides an automated invoice-to-payments platform that enables enterprise clients to streamline accounts receivable with flexible payment options. YC S22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://tranch.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/tranch

Tranch is an invoice-to-payments platform designed to help enterprises optimize cash flow and accelerate accounts receivable. Operating out of London and New York City, the company provides automated payment workflows tailored for services firms, software providers, and marketplaces.

Its platform supports a variety of payment methods, including Pay Now via FedNow, Pay by Card, Pay by Crypto, and Pay Later options ranging from 2 to 12 months for amounts up to $1 million. Tranch participated in the Y Combinator Summer 2022 batch and raised backing from investors including Global Founders Capital, TracVC, UpHonest Capital, Soma Capital, and FoundersX.

Tranch has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"What payment options does Tranch support for enterprise invoice settlement?"

"Tranch allows buyers to pay invoices immediately via FedNow, card, or cryptocurrency. It also provides a Pay Later option with flexible terms from 2 to 12 months for amounts up to $1 million."

nodes.title: Raycast
nodes.description: Raycast speeds up non-coding tasks for engineering teams. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://raycast.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/raycast

Raycast is a productivity tool that helps engineering teams reduce time spent on non‑coding tasks across common apps such as Jira, GitHub, and Slack. It targets the portion of a developer’s day—up to half—that can be consumed by coordination and administrative work.
By providing a unified command interface, Raycast lets engineers trigger actions in those services without leaving their primary workflow, which speeds up routine processes and improves overall efficiency. The company, part of the Winter 2020 batch, operates with a 27‑person team based in London and remote locations.

_Usage:_

"Does Raycast replace the native integrations in Jira, GitHub, and Slack?"

"Raycast doesn’t replace those integrations; it offers a single command palette that lets engineers invoke the same actions across the apps from one place, reducing context‑switching and saving time on non‑coding work."

nodes.title: Kontigo
nodes.description: Kontigo is a USDC‑smart neobank for Latinos. YC S24.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://kontigo.lat/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/kontigo

Kontigo is a USDC‑smart neobank targeting Latinos in the U.S. and Latin America. It launched a peer‑to‑peer onramp 20 days ago, already attracting $540k in deposits, 10,000 active users and a waitlist of over 300,000. The startup, backed by DST Global, Soma Capital, Pioneer Fund, Transpose and 10 YC alumni, is built by a team that has scaled fintechs across Latin America.

The company tackles the region’s fragmented payments landscape, where cross‑border transfers can cost up to 20% and currency depreciation runs rampant. Kontigo offers a USDC global wallet and a Bitcoin‑backed savings account, letting users send money across 33 countries without limits. Each wallet is linked to an AI‑private banker on WhatsApp that executes international USDC transactions, combining the simplicity of Venmo or Zelle with the stability of a non‑inflationary digital asset.

_Usage:_

"How does Kontigo handle cross‑border transfers compared to traditional banks?"

"Kontigo uses a USDC global wallet and a Bitcoin‑backed savings account to send money across 33 countries without limits, avoiding the up‑to‑20% fees typical of traditional cross‑border payments."

Rocket Money, formerly known as Truebill, is a personal finance application designed to analyze user spending habits and identify financial inefficiencies. The platform offers tools to optimize spending, manage subscriptions, lower bills, and automatically set aside funds for savings goals. Since its launch in 2016, the service has saved members more than $100 million.

Headquartered in Silver Spring, Maryland, with additional offices in San Francisco, the company has grown to a team of 225 people. It was backed by Accel, Bessemer Venture Partners, Eldridge Industries, and Y Combinator. Truebill was acquired, marking a significant milestone for the YC W16 company.

_Usage:_

"How does Rocket Money actually help users save money compared to just tracking expenses?"

"It goes beyond passive tracking by actively identifying inefficiencies in your financial life. The app analyzes your spending habits to find areas where you can cut costs, such as managing recurring subscriptions or negotiating lower bills. It also automates the process of setting aside money for specific savings goals, giving you a more hands-on approach to improving your financial health rather than just viewing a dashboard of past transactions."

nodes.title: Paystack
nodes.description: Modern payments infrastructure enabling businesses across Africa to accept card and mobile money transactions. YC W16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.paystack.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/paystack

Paystack provides payment processing infrastructure that allows businesses to accept credit card, debit card, money transfer, and mobile money payments directly from their websites or mobile applications. The company operates out of offices in Lagos and San Francisco, serving as a key financial tool for the African market.

Founded in Y Combinator’s Winter 2016 batch, Paystack has grown into a team of approximately 115 people. Its focus on integrating diverse local payment methods with global card networks addresses specific challenges in the region's financial ecosystem.

The company’s status is listed as Acquired, indicating it was subsequently bought by another entity, marking a significant milestone in its history as a YC alum.

_Usage:_

"How does Paystack handle the mix of local and international payment methods for merchants?"

"Paystack aggregates credit card, debit card, money transfer, and mobile money into a single integration, allowing merchants to accept these various forms of payment directly from their website or mobile app without needing separate processors for each method."

nodes.title: Axiom

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://axiom.trade | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/axiom

Axiom operates a decentralized finance trading platform that lets users trade memecoins, perpetual contracts, and earn yield on crypto assets. Since its launch the company has reached $10 million in monthly recurring revenue and generates $5 million in monthly net profit, highlighting strong demand for its niche trading services. The San Francisco‑based team of two focuses on serving fintech and consumer finance customers within the crypto/Web3 space.

_Usage:_

"How can Axiom sustain $5 million in monthly net profit with a team of only two people?"

"Axiom’s profit comes from the high‑volume trading of memecoins, perpetuals, and yield products on its platform, which has driven $10 million in monthly recurring revenue; the small team likely relies on automated systems and the efficiencies of a digital‑only service to keep operating costs low."

nodes.title: Sable
nodes.description: Sable offers a mobile banking platform that lets new-to-America internationals open U.S. accounts and build credit without an SSN. YC S19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.sablecard.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/sable

Sable is a digital banking platform that provides the only full‑suite banking solution for internationals in the United States. It offers U.S. bank accounts, debit and credit cards, and lets users open an account in as little as five minutes. Newcomers can start building a U.S. credit history from day one, even without a Social Security Number or prior U.S. credit history. The Sable app is available on iOS and Android, and the company is based in New York City with a team of 12. Sable was acquired after its Summer 2019 Y Combinator batch, reflecting its notable position in the fintech and consumer‑finance space.

_Usage:_

"Can I get a credit card from Sable without having an SSN?"

"Yes. Sable issues both debit and credit cards to eligible users who don’t have a Social Security Number, allowing them to open an account and begin building U.S. credit immediately."

nodes.title: Reflect
nodes.description: Reflect provides a no-code platform for automated website testing. YC S20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://reflect.run | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/reflect

Reflect is a no-code tool that enables companies to run automated end‑to‑end tests of web applications without writing code. By replacing complex Selenium test scripts with a visual interface, it lets engineering, product, and design teams create and maintain tests more easily.

Reflect was acquired, highlighting its value in the B2B developer‑tools market. The company, based in Villanova, PA, has a six‑person team and serves B2B, engineering, product, and design customers.

_Usage:_

"How does Reflect differ from using Selenium for website test automation?"

"Reflect offers a visual, no‑code environment for building end‑to‑end tests, so users don’t need to write or maintain Selenium code. It streamlines test creation for product and design teams, whereas Selenium requires programming expertise to script and manage tests."

nodes.title: Slash
nodes.description: Slash provides a global business banking platform with corporate cards, expense tools, and stablecoin payments. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.slash.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/slash

Slash is America’s leading business banking platform, serving over 5,000 mid‑market companies and processing $30 billion of transactions each year across all payment rails. Backed by NEA, Menlo Ventures, Stanford University and the founders of Tinder and Plaid, the company offers deposit accounts with free outgoing wire and ACH transfers, unlimited virtual cards that earn up to 2 % cash back, and integrations with major accounting platforms. It also supplies free invoicing, expense management, bill‑pay software, stablecoin payments, and a powerful card‑creation and payments API, all available to businesses in more than 100 countries. With a team of about 70 people in San Francisco, Slash positions itself as the “Costco” of business banking, delivering high cash‑back rewards and high‑yield treasury accounts while keeping its software stack free for finance teams.

_Usage:_

"How does Slash’s cashback on virtual cards compare to typical business credit cards?"

"Slash offers unlimited virtual cards with up to 2 % cash back, which is higher than the cashback rates most traditional business credit cards provide, and the cash back is combined with free expense‑management software, making the overall value proposition stronger for mid‑market firms."

nodes.title: Hilos
nodes.description: Hilos offers a no‑code platform that lets startups and SMBs run their entire business and automate customer interactions on WhatsApp. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://hilos.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/quid

Hilos provides a platform built on the WhatsApp API that enables startups and small‑to‑medium businesses to profile leads, automate follow‑ups, and integrate with tools such as CRMs, databases, and payment providers. The service is designed to run a business on WhatsApp without writing code, allowing companies to build apps directly inside the messaging app.

The company was acquired after its Summer 2021 Y Combinator batch, highlighting the market interest in low‑code messaging solutions for B2B marketing and productivity. With a five‑person team based in Mexico City and remote workers, Hilos serves the B2B and marketing industries as a SaaS messaging platform.

_Usage:_

"Is Hilos just another wrapper around the WhatsApp Business API, or does it add unique capabilities?"

"Hilos adds a no‑code layer that lets businesses profile leads, automate follow‑ups, and connect WhatsApp conversations to external systems like CRMs, databases, and payment providers, which goes beyond a simple API wrapper."

nodes.title: Level
nodes.description: Level provides fast, simple financing for lending startups. YC S21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://trylevel.app | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/level

Level offers fast and simple financing to lending startups, buying loans in small quantities and expanding access to capital as customers perform well. Within four weeks of launching, it purchased $1.3 million in loans across six customers, demonstrating rapid scaling. The company was acquired after its early traction and is backed by Liquid2, Y Combinator (S21) and others.

_Usage:_

"How is Level’s financing model different from traditional venture debt?"

"Level buys existing loans from startups in small batches and rewards good performance with additional capital, rather than providing a fixed non‑dilutive loan upfront like many venture‑debt firms. This approach lets it grow the credit line as the borrower proves itself."

nodes.title: Pulse
nodes.description: Pulse runs a crowdsourced knowledge marketplace that connects technology C‑suite executives with vendors. YC W18.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.pulse.qa | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/pulse-2

Pulse builds a crowdsourced knowledge marketplace for C‑Suite technology executives and the vendors that serve them. With nearly 15,000 executives on the platform and hundreds added daily, the service aims to change how B2B decisions are made. Companies such as Salesforce, Microsoft, Okta and Dialpad rely on Pulse to support their strategy, content and marketing teams.

Pulse was acquired, underscoring its impact on the enterprise knowledge space. The company, founded in YC’s Winter 2018 batch, operates out of San Francisco with a team of 11.

_Usage:_

"How is Pulse different from traditional analyst firms like Gartner?"

"Pulse uses a crowdsourced model where technology executives contribute insights, whereas Gartner relies on its own research analysts. This lets Pulse provide real‑time, peer‑driven advice that vendors such as Salesforce and Microsoft can tap into daily."

nodes.title: Landed
nodes.description: Provides white-labeled shared appreciation down-payment programs for employers. YC W16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.landed.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/landed

Landed offers white-labeled shared appreciation down-payment programs that let employers give employees a path to homeownership. It unlocks shared appreciation to create tailored down-payment plans that benefit both funders and buyers, and helps firms attract and keep talent.

By recycling capital as buyers exit the program, Landed builds a self-renewing pool that keeps costs low and expands access. The company was acquired, underscoring its traction in fintech and proptech.

With a lean team of two based in San Francisco and remote, Landed operates at the intersection of credit, lending, and real-estate technology.

_Usage:_

"How does Landed's shared appreciation model differ from a traditional down payment assistance program?"

"Unlike other programs, shared appreciation is mutually beneficial to funders and buyers, creating a self-renewing pool of capital that recycles as homebuyers exit the program."

nodes.title: Emburse
nodes.description: Provides corporate expense management and AP automation through issueable payment cards. YC W16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.emburse.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/emburse

Emburse is a San Francisco-based fintech platform offering expense management and accounts payable automation. The system gives businesses greater visibility and control over corporate spending by enabling them to deploy customizable payment cards.

Businesses can issue virtual or physical MasterCard-network branded expense cards directly to employees or contractors. This setup allows companies to authorize only pre-approved business expenses. The company participated in the Winter 2016 Y Combinator batch and has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does Emburse enforce corporate spending controls prior to purchase?"

"Emburse allows companies to issue physical or virtual MasterCard-network cards directly to employees and contractors. Authorization is tied to the card itself, ensuring transactions are limited to pre-approved business expenses rather than relying entirely on post-purchase reconciliation."

nodes.title: MineralSoft
nodes.description: Provides a data management platform for oil and gas mineral rights and royalty management. YC W16.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://mineralsoft.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/mineralsoft

MineralSoft is a data management platform built specifically for oil and gas mineral rights and royalty management. Based in Austin, Texas, and launching as part of the Y Combinator Winter 2016 batch, the company combines specialized software with professional services to help asset owners track and optimize their energy holdings.

The platform caters to a wide spectrum of clients managing oil and gas interests, including investment funds, family offices, individual owners, and financial advisors. It aims to streamline administrative oversight and help users maximize the value of their energy portfolios.

MineralSoft has since been acquired. Prior to its acquisition, the company grew to a team of 35 employees.

_Usage:_

"Who uses MineralSoft and what does the platform actually provide?"

"MineralSoft is designed for investment funds, family offices, individual owners, and advisors who manage oil and gas interests. Rather than being purely self-serve software, the platform pairs its specialized data management tools for mineral rights and royalties with professional services to assist users with asset management."

nodes.title: Peer5
nodes.description: Builds a peer-to-peer content delivery network that optimizes live and on-demand video streaming. YC W17.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.peer5.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/peer5

Peer5 provides a peer-to-peer (P2P) content delivery network (CDN) designed to improve live and on-demand video streams. As video quality shifts toward HD and 4K, traditional CDNs can struggle with peak demand, forcing publishers to pay for underutilized server capacity. Peer5 works alongside existing servers, offloading bandwidth to a peer network so that the delivery network grows stronger as viewership increases. Peer5 has since been acquired.

The service leverages HTML5 and WebRTC, enabling P2P delivery inside end-user web browsers without requiring software or plugin installations. It integrates with content providers' existing setups and supports various streaming protocols, players, and media servers. On average, Peer5 offloads 70% of bandwidth, increases server capacity by 20x, extends viewing time by 30%, and decreases rebuffering instances by 40%.

_Usage:_

"How does Peer5's P2P delivery work without forcing end users to install a client or plugin?"

"Peer5 relies on native web technologies like WebRTC and HTML5, allowing peer-to-peer bandwidth sharing directly inside standard web browsers with zero installation required from viewers. It acts as an overlay on top of existing media servers and traditional CDNs, supporting a wide range of streaming protocols and players to offload up to 70% of peak bandwidth onto the peer network."

nodes.title: Preflight
nodes.description: Builds a no-code automated web and API testing platform that adapts to UI changes. YC W19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://preflight.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/preflight

Preflight is a no-code web testing platform designed to simplify creating and maintaining test suites. It claims to be 20x faster than manually writing tests in Selenium or Cypress. To address brittle test maintenance, Preflight interprets web pages as human users understand them, adapting to structural changes and automatically updating selectors whenever a test passes.

Beyond basic UI automation, Preflight includes a Workflow feature for orchestrating dependent end-to-end test sequences. It also streamlines API test creation by prepopulating API tests directly from the network calls captured during UI test execution, enabling teams to set up API tests in minutes.

Preflight was part of the Y Combinator Winter 2019 batch and operated with a team in Chicago and remotely. The company has since been acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does Preflight handle UI test maintenance compared to traditional frameworks like Selenium or Cypress?"

"Unlike traditional Selenium and Cypress setups that require manual selector updates whenever the UI changes, Preflight interprets web pages the way human users do. It adapts to design changes automatically and updates selectors whenever a test succeeds. Additionally, it accelerates backend testing by prepopulating API tests using the network calls captured during UI testing."

The marketplace pairs integrated data management and collaboration tools, allowing customers to search, select, purchase, assemble, and manage data sets for faster and more accurate planning.

"Geosite’s marketplace aggregates both public and commercial satellite imagery and sensor data into a single, searchable repository. It couples this data with integrated management and collaboration tools, so users can not only find and purchase data but also assemble and manage it within the same platform."

nodes.title: Fly.io
nodes.description: Run full stack apps close to your users. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://fly.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fly-io

Fly.io is a cloud infrastructure platform that lets developers run full‑stack applications close to their users. It offers a simple deployment model where a Docker image can be pushed to Fly.io and the platform automatically provisions app servers and databases in the regions that matter most. The service is designed to reduce latency and improve performance for end users worldwide.

Founded in Winter 2020, Fly.io has grown to a team of 48 engineers based in Chicago and remote. It focuses on B2B infrastructure and provides a CLI that simplifies the process of launching and scaling instances. Fly.io’s approach is notable for its emphasis on geographic proximity and ease of deployment for full‑stack workloads.

_Usage:_

"How does Fly.io’s deployment model differ from traditional cloud providers like AWS or Azure?"

"Fly.io’s CLI lets developers launch instances in specific regions with a single command, automatically provisioning app servers and databases close to end users, which simplifies the deployment of full‑stack Docker images compared to the more complex orchestration required on AWS or Azure."

nodes.title: Loop Health
nodes.description: Loop Health offers modern, comprehensive health insurance plans for employees in India. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.loophealth.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/loop-health

Loop Health is a new type of healthcare provider that combines high‑quality primary care with employer‑funded insurance. Employees receive unlimited primary care visits at asset‑light clinics, along with traditional hospitalization coverage.
During its YC Winter 2020 batch, Loop grew from zero to $85,000 ARR with 200% month‑over‑month growth, serving 22 companies and 5,500 members in Pune. Employers pay $15 per member per year for the base plan and Loop earns an additional $25 on prescriptions, lab tests, and hospitalization referrals, yielding 70% gross margins.
The company addresses a gap in the Indian market where only 8% of employees use hospital‑only insurance benefits. By offering doctor visits and telemedicine at the same price, Loop can lower premiums while giving employees better access to care, tapping into a $8 billion, 27% CAGR employer‑funded health insurance opportunity.

_Usage:_

"How does Loop Health's pricing structure differ from traditional employer health plans?"

"Loop Health charges employers $15 per member per year for the base plan, which includes unlimited primary care visits and traditional hospitalization coverage. The company also earns an additional $25 on each prescription, lab test, or hospitalization referral, resulting in a 70% gross margin. This structure keeps overall costs comparable to traditional plans while providing more comprehensive coverage."

nodes.title: delt.ai
nodes.description: Digital banking for businesses in Latam. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://delt.ai | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/delt-ai

delt.ai is building a specialized digital financial service for businesses in Latam, aiming to tackle the more than 450 B market of business payments in Mexico. The company is a natively digital alternative to a bank, built from the ground up with payment gateways and API integrations. Its fully digital, KYC‑compliant onboarding enabled it to become the first to open branchless accounts in the country, targeting poorly served startups and SMEs and focusing on the roughly 40 B market opportunity that is profitable when served fully online. delt.ai was acquired.

The startup operates out of Mexico City with a team of 26 employees and focuses on the fintech and banking and exchange industries.

_Usage:_

"How does delt.ai’s branchless account onboarding differ from traditional banks?"

"delt.ai’s onboarding is fully digital and KYC‑compliant, allowing it to open branchless accounts in Mexico—a first for the country."

nodes.title: Savvy

nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.gosavvy.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/savvy-2

Savvy is a health benefits product that gives employees payment cards to purchase their own health insurance, providing a flexible stipend model. The company grew to tens of millions in volume and expanded into all 50 U.S. state health insurance markets, becoming one of the first to market after new regulation. In 2022, Savvy was acquired by Take Command, the leading incumbent in the health insurance HRA space, after receiving backing from Y Combinator, Marc Andreessen, and the founders of One Medical and Indeed.

Savvy operates with a team of 12 in San Francisco and focuses on fintech and insurance solutions.

"Savvy’s model gives employees a payment card that they can use to buy their own health insurance plans, instead of the employer paying premiums directly; this allows employees to choose plans that best fit their needs and gives them more control over their benefits."

nodes.body:
**Website:** http://www.viyaliving.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/viya

Viya operated a mobile-first platform for apartment rentals in Latin America, focusing on making city-center living more affordable and convenient. The company offered room and apartment leases paired with seamless services such as cleaning, maintenance, laundry, and dry cleaning to reduce the burden on tenants.

Based in Monterrey, Mexico, the team of 22 had backgrounds from MIT and real estate, aiming to improve the rental experience for both tenants and owners through technology. At its peak, the company reported a monthly recurring revenue of $60k growing at 20% weekly with 40% margins.

Viya is now listed as inactive in the YC directory, indicating that the company has since shut down.

"Instead of just listing properties, Viya bundled the lease with essential services like cleaning, maintenance, and laundry. This approach was designed to make living in city centers more affordable and less hectic for tenants by handling the operational friction of renting, rather than just providing a space."

nodes.title: Edlyft
nodes.description: Software for enterprises to train college CS students on essential job skills before hiring. YC W20.
nodes.body:
**Website:** http://edlyft.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/edlyft

Edlyft built software that allowed blue-chip enterprises to train college computer science students on essential workforce skills, aiming to make new graduates productive from day one. The company addressed the common issue where new grad engineers take six to twelve months to ramp up, offering an alternative to relying solely on experienced engineers for onboarding. Notable users included Google, Dropbox, Tinder, and LinkedIn, who utilized the platform to prepare students for their specific roles prior to hiring.

Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Kapor Capital, and Y Combinator, Edlyft operated with a small team of five based in San Francisco and remote locations. The company was founded by CS graduates from Yale and Stanford who had previously worked at Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, and Bain. Edlyft has since become inactive.

_Usage:_

"How does Edlyft reduce the time it takes for new grad engineers to become productive?"

"Instead of waiting for new hires to ramp up on the job over six to twelve months, Edlyft trains college CS students on essential skills before they are hired. This allows enterprises to onboard candidates who are already prepared for the specific requirements of the role, reducing the initial salary cost associated with training inexperienced engineers."

nodes.title: Jiga
nodes.description: Source high-quality, cost-competitive custom parts faster by partnering directly with vetted manufacturers. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://jiga.io | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/jiga

Jiga enables engineers and supply chain managers to source high-quality, cost-competitive custom parts by partnering directly with vetted manufacturers. nodes.title: UPchieve
nodes.description: Provides free, 24/7 online tutoring to low-income high school students via a live volunteer matching app. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.upchieve.org | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/upchieve

UPchieve is an edtech nonprofit that connects low-income high school students with free, 24/7 online tutoring. The platform addresses a significant gap in academic support by pairing students with live volunteers in under five minutes through its mobile application.

The organization targets the approximately 8 million low-income high school students in the US who lack in-home help with schoolwork. By democratizing access to academic support, UPchieve aims to provide equal opportunities for college attendance and upward mobility. To date, the platform has matched over 100,000 tutoring requests.

Based in New York City with a remote-friendly team of 15, UPchieve continues to operate as an active nonprofit focused on educational equity.

_Usage:_

"How does UPchieve handle the logistics of providing 24/7 tutoring without a massive paid staff?"

"UPchieve relies on a network of volunteers rather than paid tutors. When a student requests help through the app, the system matches them with an available live volunteer in under five minutes, allowing the nonprofit to scale its 24/7 coverage using community resources instead of a large payroll."

nodes.title: peopleCQ

nodes.body:

The company focuses on four core pillars: saving, spending, budgeting, and borrowing, aiming to improve each aspect through specialized products.

The platform allows employees to receive their salaries in advance at any point during the month and pay bills instantly. Founded by ex-employees of major tech and telecom firms, the company has raised $3.7 million from investors including 500 Startups, Beco Capital, and Plug and Play.

With a team of 85, peopleCQ positions itself as a comprehensive solution for employee financial health in the Egyptian market.

_Usage:_

"Employees can access their earned salaries in advance at any time during the month, rather than waiting for the standard payroll date. This is part of a broader suite that also includes instant bill payment, designed to give workers more control over their cash flow."

nodes.title: Worksphere
nodes.description: Manage hybrid workplace logistics by allowing employees to reserve desks and see who is in the office. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.worksphere.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/worksphere

Worksphere provides a platform for companies to manage hybrid work environments where staff split time between home and the office. It enables employees to reserve specific desks, view which colleagues are present, and coordinate in-person meetings more effectively.

The solution allows organizations to optimize their real estate usage by identifying and releasing unused office space, thereby reducing overhead costs. The company, based in Seattle, operated as a small team of six before being acquired.

_Usage:_

"How does Worksphere actually help a company save money on office space if it's just a desk booking tool?"

"It helps by providing visibility into actual desk utilization and who is in the office. This data allows companies to downsize their physical footprint by letting go of unused space, rather than paying for empty desks that are only needed on specific days."

nodes.title: OctiFi
nodes.description: Buy Now Pay Later platform offering 0% interest loans for home renovation and furniture purchases in Southeast Asia. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.octifi.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/octifi

OctiFi provides a Buy Now Pay Later service tailored for the Southeast Asian market, specifically Singapore. The platform empowers commerce by offering instant 0% interest loans to responsible spenders, enabling consumers to finance larger purchases such as home renovations or online furniture without incurring extra costs.

The company operated with a team of 11 and focused on consumer finance within the fintech industry. OctiFi has since been acquired, marking the conclusion of its independent operations.

_Usage:_

"How does OctiFi's 0% interest BNPL model differ from standard credit card financing for large purchases like home renovations?"

"OctiFi offers instant loans with 0% interest specifically for responsible spenders, allowing users to pay later at no extra cost. This contrasts with standard credit card financing, which typically accrues interest on the balance if not paid in full, making OctiFi's model a cost-neutral option for extending budget on items like furniture or renovation projects."

nodes.title: Bueno Finance
nodes.description: Building a digital credit card platform over UPI for India's next billion users. YC W21.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://buenofinanceinc.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/bueno-finance

Bueno Finance operates as a credit building platform designed for the next billion users in India. The company offers a digital credit card that functions over the UPI payment network, aiming to make credit accessible to a broader demographic. It was founded in Winter 2021 and is based in Gurugram, India.

The company has since been acquired, marking a significant milestone in its trajectory within the Indian fintech sector. With a team of 18, Bueno Finance focused on the intersection of neobanking and credit lending to serve underserved markets.

_Usage:_

"How does Bueno Finance integrate credit with India's existing payment infrastructure?"

"Bueno Finance issues a digital credit card that operates directly over UPI, the Unified Payments Interface. This allows users to build credit history through standard UPI transactions rather than relying on traditional bank-issued cards, effectively leveraging the existing payment rails for credit access."

nodes.title: Common Paper
nodes.description: Common Paper offers open‑source, standardized contracts that let startups close sales deals faster. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://commonpaper.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/common-paper

Common Paper is a contracting platform that helps startups close deals with customers faster and with less risk. It creates standard, open‑source contracts for commercial transactions—including NDAs, DPAs, and sales agreements—analogous to the SAFE but for vendor‑customer relationships. The standardized format structures contract data from inception, and the company builds software for managing these contracts, accelerating sales cycles, and making contract data programmatically accessible to other business systems. Tens of thousands of users have downloaded the contracts, and 63 % of the contracts on its system close within 24 hours. The company, part of the Winter 2023 batch, has a team of eight and operates from Philadelphia and remotely.

_Usage:_

"How does Common Paper’s open‑source contract format make a sales deal close faster than a custom‑drafted agreement?"

"Because the contracts are standardized and structured from the start, the platform can automatically fill, track, and exchange the necessary terms, letting both parties sign and execute the agreement without the back‑and‑forth of drafting a custom document, which is why 63 % of its contracts close within 24 hours."

nodes.title: Invopop
nodes.description: Invopop provides a single API that lets global software companies handle electronic invoicing and tax reporting in over 25 countries. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.invopop.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/invopop

Invopop enables global software firms such as SumUp, Fever, and DeepL to manage electronic invoicing across more than 25 jurisdictions through one unified API. By connecting once to Invopop, companies avoid the complexity of building and maintaining separate local integrations for each tax authority, streamlining compliance and saving time. The service is positioned for a market where, in the next five years, over 40 countries—including all EU members—will mandate real‑time electronic invoicing and reporting.

With a team of seven based in Madrid, Invopop targets B2B finance and accounting needs, helping firms meet upcoming regulatory requirements without extensive in‑house development.

_Usage:_

"How does using Invopop compare to building our own country‑specific invoicing integrations?"

"Invopop offers a single API that already supports electronic invoicing and real‑time tax reporting for more than 25 countries, so you only need one integration instead of maintaining dozens of separate connections. This reduces development effort and ongoing maintenance, letting you comply with upcoming EU mandates without building each local solution yourself."

nodes.title: Railbird
nodes.description: A prediction market exchange for hedging risk in the services sector. YC W22.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.railbirdexchange.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/railbird

Railbird built a prediction market exchange specifically designed to help the services sector hedge and mitigate financial risk. The platform targeted volatile industries such as hospitality, tourism, recreation, entertainment, and sports, where traditional risk-hedging opportunities were scarce. By opening the exchange to all traders, Railbird aimed to provide a more liquid and accessible way to manage uncertainty in these markets.

The company, based in New York City with a team of eight, operated in the fintech and marketplace space. It was notably acquired, marking the end of its independent operations as a YC-backed startup.

_Usage:_

"How does Railbird differ from general prediction markets like Polymarket or Kalshi?"

"While general prediction markets focus on broad political or cultural events, Railbird was specifically engineered for the services sector. It allowed traders to hedge against volatility in industries like hospitality and tourism, providing a financial instrument tailored to business risk rather than just speculative event outcomes."

nodes.title: Alaan
nodes.description: AI-native finance platform for Middle Eastern businesses combining cards, banking, and accounting. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.alaan.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/alaan

Alaan is an AI-native finance platform designed to simplify financial operations for businesses in the Middle East. Launched in August 2022, the company consolidates corporate cards, business bank accounts, international transfers, expense management, and accounting automation into a single interface. The platform integrates intelligence into every finance workflow to streamline processes for its users.

Headquartered in Dubai, Alaan has grown rapidly to serve over 3,000 startups, mid-market, and enterprise customers. The company processes tens of millions of dollars in monthly payment volume and has raised one of the largest Series A rounds in Middle East history, backed by Peak XV. As a fintech company rather than a bank, Alaan issues its business bank accounts through a partnership with ruya.

_Usage:_

"How does Alaan handle the banking aspect if it isn't a licensed bank itself?"

"Alaan operates as a fintech company, not a bank. While it provides the interface for business bank accounts, the actual accounts are issued by a partner named ruya. This allows Alaan to offer banking features alongside its other tools like corporate cards and expense management without holding a banking license itself."

nodes.description: A single payment platform that simplifies EV charging transactions and expense management for drivers and fleets. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://thebluedot.co/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/bluedot

Bluedot operates as a unified payment infrastructure for electric vehicle charging, addressing the lack of standardized payment and expense management tools in the growing EV market. The company launched its Bluedot card in December 2022, leveraging a team with strong fintech backgrounds to handle the transactional complexity of EV usage for both individual drivers and commercial fleets.

The startup is based in San Francisco and has a team of 15 members. It secured pre-seed funding from Y Combinator, Axel Springer, Porsche, Ford, TechNexus, DRF, and Pritchard Automotive. The company reported rapid growth, citing a 40-45% weekly increase and $110K in GMV in the week prior to its directory entry.

_Usage:_

"How does Bluedot handle the payment side of EV charging compared to existing fragmented solutions?"

"Bluedot acts as a single payment platform that consolidates the process of paying for EV charging and managing associated expenses. Instead of dealing with multiple networks or manual expense tracking, users utilize the Bluedot card to streamline transactions for both personal driving and fleet operations, effectively filling a gap in the payments management infrastructure for the electric vehicle sector."

nodes.body:

nodes.title: Versori
nodes.description: Agentic integrations & automations for enterprise. YC W23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.versori.com/ | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/versori

Versori builds a platform that lets product, operations, and GTM teams create custom integrations, workflows, and agents quickly. It offers a low-code SDK and full-code options, enabling teams to deliver integrations in days instead of months. The platform includes proactive, self-healing agents that monitor connected apps for changes and automatically fix them. Versori targets B2B infrastructure customers and emphasizes limitless customization compared to embedded IPaaS solutions that lock into connector limits. Its speed to value can cut typical deployment fees by half or more, and its managed custom-builds allow sales teams to satisfy any prospect’s integration request without delays. Versori was acquired in 2023, reflecting its traction in the enterprise integration space. The company is based in Manchester, England, and employs 16 people.

_Usage:_

"How does Versori differ from traditional low-code integration platforms?"

"Versori offers proactive, self-healing agents that monitor and fix endpoint or schema changes automatically, unlike most low-code platforms that require manual updates. It also provides a flexible SDK for embedding custom integrations and full-code control, giving teams more customization than typical IPaaS solutions."

nodes.title: Legacy
nodes.description: Legacy helps you test, improve, and freeze your sperm. YC S19.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://www.givelegacy.com | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/legacy

Legacy is a startup focused on fertility and family planning, offering a mail‑in kit for sperm testing and freezing, personalized improvement products, tele‑health, DNA fragmentation analysis, and supplements. It aims to change the outdated view that fertility is a women's issue by making the process accessible and affordable for men and people with sperm.

Founded at Harvard, Legacy has raised $40M from investors including FirstMark Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, Section 32, Tribe Capital, and celebrities such as Justin Bieber and The Weeknd. It has secured nationwide insurance coverage for over 10 million lives, military contracts including the Navy SEALs and 15 million veterans, and employer offerings with top fertility benefit providers.

With a team of about 30, the company emphasizes values such as customer centricity, reliability, kindness, openness, and winning, and operates out of New York City and Cambridge, Massachusetts.

_Usage:_

"What makes Legacy's sperm testing kit more convenient than traditional lab tests?"

"Legacy's kit is a mail‑in service that delivers DNA fragmentation analysis and personalized improvement products, making the process more affordable and accessible for men and people with sperm."

nodes.title: refine
nodes.description: Refine is an open‑source Retool for enterprise web applications. YC S23.
nodes.body:
**Website:** https://refine.dev | **YC:** https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/refine

Refine is a headless React framework that lets teams build enterprise web applications quickly. It removes repetitive tasks such as CRUD, state management, routing, authentication, access control, and i18n, saving developers days of work.

Since its launch, thousands of projects have been built by more than 15,000 monthly active developers. The community has grown to 16,000 GitHub stars, over 180 contributors, and 2,500 Discord members, reflecting its popularity among B2B, engineering, and product‑design teams.

Refine’s headless UI approach means it works with any custom design and ships with ready‑made integrations for Ant Design, Material UI, Chakra UI, and Mantine. It is backend‑agnostic and can connect to more than 15 backend services out of the box, including custom REST and GraphQL APIs, giving developers full control over styling and deployment.

_Usage:_

"How does refine handle authentication compared to other React admin frameworks?"

"Refine eliminates the need to write authentication boilerplate by providing built‑in support for authentication and access control. It works with any backend, so developers can plug in custom REST or GraphQL endpoints or use third‑party auth services, giving the same level of flexibility as other frameworks but with less setup time."

nodes.body:
**LinkedIn:** linkedin.com/in/johnramunas

John Ramunas, PhD, invented TERT mRNA telomere extension at Stanford in Helen Blau's lab — reversing a decade of telomere shortening in one treatment. 50+ granted patents across 7 families through 2046. Preclinical efficacy in 4 organ systems. FDA INTERACT cleared. Khosla Ventures seed. YC S18. Raising $10M seed extension ($2M wired) for 3 clinical trials — Phase I readout Q3 2027. nodes.title: Antony Samuel
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Artifact, a collaborative AI-native IDE for hardware engineers.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Artifact](./Artifact.md) with [Corbin Klett](./Corbin%20Klett.md), building what the pair call "the VS Code for hardware engineers" — a collaborative workspace for electrical system design. Samuel is a Georgia Tech-trained electrical engineer with eight years developing avionics and software for complex aerospace systems, most recently as Avionics Lead at Hermeus, where he built the team behind the avionics for the world's fastest aircraft (Mach 5).

_Usage:_

"What frustration led to Artifact?"

"Antony Samuel and Corbin Klett both worked on outdated hardware design tools during their aerospace careers — Samuel on Mach 5 aircraft avionics at Hermeus — and built Artifact as the collaborative, version-controlled tool they wished they'd had."

nodes.title: Ahmed Abdulaal
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Mecha Health, foundation models automating x-ray analysis for radiologists.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Mecha Health](./Mecha%20Health.md) with Hugo Fry, Nina Montaña Brown, and Ayodeji Ijishakin, building foundation models that produce accurate draft radiology reports from medical images. Abdulaal trained in medicine at Imperial College London and is a Microsoft PhD scholar at UCL, having previously worked as a Research Scientist at AstraZeneca's Center for Artificial Intelligence. nodes.title: Peter Tribelhorn
nodes.description: Co-founder of Hera, an AI motion design platform.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Hera](./Hera.md) with [Chia-Lun Wu](./Chia-Lun%20Wu.md), building an AI tool that makes motion design radically faster and cheaper — users have created over 50,000 animations, with more than 200,000 created in the first two weeks after launch. Before Hera, Tribelhorn worked in investment banking after studying at WHU, then joined Lunar X, where he acquired and scaled YouTube channels like Economics Explained and The Game Theorists to over 30 million subscribers, repeatedly hitting the same bottleneck: slow, expensive animation production.

_Usage:_

"What inspired Peter Tribelhorn to start Hera?"

"While scaling YouTube channels with tens of millions of subscribers at Lunar X, he kept hitting the same bottleneck — animation was slow and expensive — which became the problem Hera was built to solve."

nodes.title: Marius Montmany
nodes.description: Co-founder of REVER, an e-commerce returns and refunds platform.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [REVER](./REVER.md) in 2022 with [Oriol Hernandez i Fajula](./Oriol%20Hernandez%20i%20Fajula.md) in Barcelona, part of YC's Summer 2022 batch, after both grew frustrated with "reverse logistics" — the difficulty of handling product returns efficiently. Co-founded [refine](./refine.md) as CEO in 2022 with [Omer Aplak](./Omer%20Aplak.md) and [Eren Erkalkan](./Eren%20Erkalkan.md), part of YC's Summer 2023 batch, building an open-source, headless React framework for rapidly building enterprise web applications. Ozseyhan is a serial entrepreneur with 15-plus years of experience building enterprise software, and previously co-founded Fixie Digital GmbH from 2016 to 2022.

_Usage:_

"What does refine offer developers?"

"An open-source, headless React framework that eliminates repetitive enterprise app work — CRUD, state management, authentication, access control, and i18n — while giving developers full control of their stack."

nodes.title: Olivier Moindrot
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Fragment, an AI workflow platform acquired by Sierra.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Fragment](./Fragment.md) as CEO, part of YC's Summer 2023 batch, helping businesses integrate AI into their workflows. Moindrot ranked first in the entrance exam at École Polytechnique and studied at Stanford, and previously created and led the AI team at MetaMap. Fragment was acquired by Bret Taylor's Sierra in April 2026, with Moindrot joining Sierra's team to strengthen its agent development in France.

_Usage:_

"What happened to Fragment?"

"Sierra, the customer-service AI agent company founded by Bret Taylor, acquired Fragment in April 2026, and Olivier Moindrot joined Sierra's team."

nodes.title: Mukund Jha
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Emergent, an AI platform that turns plain English into working apps.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Emergent](./Emergent.md) as CEO with his twin brother [Madhav Jha](./Madhav%20Jha.md), part of YC's Summer 2024 batch, building an AI-powered platform that turns plain-English descriptions into fully functional web and mobile apps without coding. Jha dropped out of a PhD program to found the company, is a graduate of Columbia Engineering, and previously co-founded and served as CTO of Dunzo. Emergent raised $100M from Khosla Ventures, SoftBank, Google, and others, reaching $50M ARR within 7 months of public launch.

_Usage:_

"How fast did Emergent grow after launch?"

"It reached $50 million in annual recurring revenue within 7 months of public launch, with over 5 million users across 190-plus countries building more than 6 million apps."

nodes.title: Mayank Mehta
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Pulse, a crowdsourced knowledge marketplace for IT executives.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Pulse](./Pulse.md) as CEO in 2017 with [Anand Thaker](./Anand%20Thaker.md) in San Francisco, part of YC's 2018 batch, building a crowdsourced knowledge marketplace connecting C-Suite technology executives with vendors. Companies including Salesforce, Microsoft, Okta, and Dialpad have relied on Pulse to inform their strategy, content, and marketing teams.

_Usage:_

"Who uses Pulse?"

"C-Suite technology executives share insights on the platform, while companies like Salesforce, Microsoft, Okta, and Dialpad use that data to inform their strategy and marketing."

nodes.title: Josh Wymer
nodes.description: Co-founder and CEO of Central, back-office software for startups, acquired by Mercury.
nodes.body:
Co-founded [Central](./Central.md) as CEO in April 2023 with [Pranav Kashyap](./Pranav%20Kashyap.md) and [Nilay Modi](./Nilay%20Modi.md), part of YC's Summer 2024 batch, consolidating payroll, benefits, state compliance, accounting, and R&D tax credits for startups. Wymer was the 12th employee at Mixpanel, where he ran product engineering and helped scale it past a $1B valuation, and also worked as a software engineer at Meta and played baseball at Virginia Tech. Central was later acquired by Mercury.
